title: Removing repo ACLs in case /tmp has them set to inherig
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Adds ACL removal logic to fix permission issues when `/tmp` has inherited ACLs. The changes address a specific edge case where `/tmp` has ACL inheritance settings that could prevent the cloned repository folder from being executable. The fix: - Removes ACL inheritance with `setfacl -k` - Clears existing ACLs with `setfacl -b` - Explicitly sets execute permissions on the repo folder **Issues Found:** - Missing error handling: `subprocess.check_output()` will crash if `setfacl` is unavailable or fails - The `acl` package is not included in `install_linux.sh` dependencies, which may cause failures on fresh installations - Minor typo: "inhereted" should be "inherited"

title: Show logged in user in frontend
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a feature to display the logged-in user's name in the frontend sidebar menu. Key changes: - **User name persistence**: Stores `user_name` in localStorage upon successful login (from API response `user_data.data._name`) and removes it on logout - **Sidebar display**: Shows the user name in a label in the sidebar menu when logged in - **Page refresh**: Automatically reloads the page after 60 seconds post login/logout to refresh the sidebar with updated user state - **Code refactoring**: Improved string concatenation in `GMTMenu` from template literal reassignment (`html_content = \`\${html_content}...\``) to `+=` operator for better efficiency **Security concern**: The `user_name` value from localStorage is inserted directly into HTML without escaping. Consider using `escapeString()` to prevent potential XSS.

title: Enforcing CPU and memory limits
body:
This PR introduces auto-set CPU and memory limits to prevent the host system from either running into OOM or getting timer issues with the Metric Providers. ## CPU Currently the GMT puts all metric providers on Core 0. This PR uses *cpuset* directives of docker to keep core 0 free. This also introduces the minium system requirement of at least having two cores available. ## Memory The host running GMT could easily OOM if the containers request too much memory. Before memory limits where optional and had no limits. With this PR GMT will now auto-assign memory limits to the extent that 1 GB is always kept unavailable to the containers. This shall save the host from getting OOM This PR is subject to change. Discussion points: - Is 1 GB a good limit? Typically GMT with the python runtime takes ~800 MB to run. So this would mean 200 MB left for the OS. Enough ...? - The set configuration is very opaque. Where to display the info best? Re-paste it to the usage scenario? Show it somewhere else? Maybe a limits/utilization tab?

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces automatic CPU and memory limits for Docker containers to prevent OOM and timing issues. The implementation reserves 1GB for GMT overhead, assigns remaining memory fairly to containers, and keeps CPU core 0 free for metric providers using `cpuset`. **Key changes:** - Adds `_populate_cpu_and_memory_limits()` function that runs before container startup - Auto-assigns memory limits by dividing available memory (total - 1GB) equally among containers without user-specified limits - Moves memory limits from `deploy.resources.limits.memory` to `mem_limit` for consistent handling - Configures cpuset to exclude core 0 from container assignment - Disables swap completely by setting `--memory-swap` equal to `--memory` - Updates system checks to require minimum 2 CPU cores and 2GB free memory - Refactors memory parsing into shared `utils.docker_memory_to_bytes()` function **Issues found:** - **Critical**: The utilization reporter at `optimization_providers/resources/utilization.py:20` only checks `deploy.resources.limits.memory`, but this is deleted and moved to `mem_limit` during processing. This will cause false warnings about missing memory limits. **Architecture notes:** - The same CPU count validation is performed twice (lines 626 and 1110), suggesting these could be deduplicated by storing the value as an instance variable - The PR correctly handles edge cases like tight memory scenarios with appropriate warnings

Added `version` field to the Eco CI v3 endpoint to track client version information. title: Backfill carbon intensity
body:
With CarbonDB now open source we now introduce also the backfill mechanism to the open source code, which was previously premium members only. - Table columns can now be null - Will be backfilled when CarbonDB cronjobs run. atm it might be confusiong that carbonDB is backfilling eco-ci .... might split out later in two separate cronjobs

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces carbon intensity backfilling from CarbonDB, allowing NULL values in `carbon_intensity_g` column that will be populated by cron jobs. **Key changes:** - Migration to allow NULL in `carbon_intensity_g` column - Backfill logic added to populate missing carbon intensity values from German grid data - API now returns NULL instead of -1 when carbon intensity unavailable - Power HOG data now passes actual grid intensity instead of placeholder -1 **Critical issues found:** - Line 67 references non-existent `carbon_ug` column (should be `carbon_kg`) - `carbon_kg` column needs to allow NULL since code sets it to None when carbon intensity unavailable - Migration incomplete - missing `carbon_kg` NULL constraint removal - `validate_table_constraints()` will fail after migration since it expects columns to be NOT NULL that are now nullable

title: Added NOT NULL to all columns where it made sense
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Added `NOT NULL` constraints to 40+ columns across multiple tables to enforce data integrity in the database schema. **Critical Issues Found:** - **Missing migration file**: Only `structure.sql` updated, no `ALTER TABLE` statements for existing databases - **Conflicting constraint**: `hog_simplified_measurements.user_id` has `NOT NULL` with `ON DELETE SET NULL` (line 637) **Concerns:** - Existing databases with NULL values in these columns will fail when migration is applied - No data validation or backfill strategy provided for tables like `machines.description`, `runs.uri`, `notes.note`, `warnings.message`, etc. - Foreign key syntax reformatted in `hog_top_processes` table (line 662)

title: CarbonDB merge window added
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Implements a 30-day merge window for CarbonDB data ingestion, rejecting timestamps older than 30 days or in the future, and updates the status code from 204 to 202 to better reflect asynchronous processing. - Adds timestamp validation in `carbondb_add()` to enforce 30-day merge window and reject future timestamps - Changes response status code from 204 (No Content) to 202 (Accepted) for `/v2/carbondb/add` endpoint, which better indicates asynchronous processing - Updates `copy_over_eco_ci()` interval from 1 to 30 days to align with new merge window policy - Adds comprehensive test coverage for boundary conditions (outdated data, at-border timestamps, future timestamps) - Minor style issues with spacing in the validation code

title: Bump psycopg[binary] from 3.3.1 to 3.3.2
body:
Bumps [psycopg[binary]](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg) from 3.3.1 to 3.3.2.
Changelog

Sourced from psycopg[binary]'s changelog.

.. currentmodule:: psycopg

.. index:: single: Release notes single: News

psycopg release notes

Current release

Psycopg 3.3.2 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Fix race condition in adapters at startup (:ticket:[#1230](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1230)).

Psycopg 3.3.1 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Fix iteration on server-side cursors (:ticket:[#1226](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1226)).

Psycopg 3.3.0

.. rubric:: New top-level features

  • Add :ref:template strings queries \<template-strings> (:ticket:[#1054](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1054)).
  • More flexible :ref:composite adaptation<adapt-composite>: it is now possible to adapt Python objects to PostgreSQL composites and back even if they are not sequences or if they take keyword arguments (:ticket:[#932](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/932), :ticket:[#1202](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1202)).
  • Cursors are now iterators_, not just iterables_. This means you can call next\ (cur) or anext\ (cur), which is useful as a :ref:type-safe expression <typing-fetchone> (:ticket:[#1064](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1064)).
  • Add Cursor.set_result() and Cursor.results() to move across the result sets of queries executed though ~Cursor.executemany() or ~Cursor.execute() with multiple statements (:tickets:[#1080](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1080), [#1170](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1170)).
  • Add :ref:transaction-status to report the status during and after a ~Connection.transaction() block (:ticket:[#969](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/969)).
  • Allow to change loaders using ~adapt.AdaptersMap.register_loader() on Cursor.adapters after a query result has been already returned (:ticket:[#884](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/884)).

title: Normalizing API to always return 202 for POST requests
Removed legacy custom key type
body:
This PR aims to remove a key we introduced a while ago to the service definition in the compose file: - `type` Currently there never was and there currently is no use for this key and thus it shall be removed as it poses rather a compatibility risk than any gain. In case it can get reintroduced. This PR will stay open for one month as RFC. If no complaings happen it will be removed.

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR removes the legacy `type` field from service definitions in usage scenario YAML files. The field was defined in the schema from the beginning but was never actually used by the system. The only valid value was `container`, which provided no functional benefit. **Key changes:** - Removed `valid_service_types()` validation method from `lib/schema_checker.py:57-62` - Removed `Optional('type'): Use(self.valid_service_types)` from the service schema in `lib/schema_checker.py:102` - Removed `type: container` lines from 57 test and example usage scenario files **Assessment:** The removal is clean and complete. No runtime code references the `type` field, and the schema validation properly rejects it as an unsupported key after this change. Since the field was never used functionally, this is a low-risk cleanup that simplifies the schema.

title: Adds a resbmit button
body: Adds a simple button to resubmit jobs if they have failed. This is useful when you have a timeout in playwright and the tests should actually work. Is only relevant for the cluster but didn't add a logic to hide on dev machines.

title: Hide broken badges
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Added `onerror` handlers to badge images that automatically hide broken badges and log debug info when they fail to load, typically due to non-public run visibility. - Updated documentation in both `stats.html` and `timeline.html` to clarify badge visibility requirements - Added error handlers in `stats.js` and `timeline.js` to remove badge DOM elements on load failure - **Critical bug**: In `timeline.js:199`, the error handler references undefined variable `metric_name` instead of `series[my_series].metric_name`, which will cause incorrect console logging - **HTML syntax error**: In `timeline.html:97-98`, list items incorrectly use `

` closing tags instead of ``

title: Sending usage scenario variables as empty or null will include all combinations
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR enhances the timeline query feature to allow viewing all usage scenario variable combinations when no specific filter is provided. **Key changes:** - Makes `usage_scenario_variables` filter conditional in `get_timeline_query()` - only applies when explicitly provided - Adds JSON validation for `usage_scenario_variables` using `orjson.loads()` before query execution - Updates the frontend with a helpful hint: "Leave empty to include all" Previously, empty/null `usage_scenario_variables` defaulted to `{}`, which would only match runs with exactly empty variables. Now, leaving it empty returns all runs regardless of their usage scenario variables, giving users more flexibility when exploring timeline data.

title: Container name resolution & Refactor metric provider c includes
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors the C metric provider codebase by consolidating duplicated container-handling code into a shared library (`gmt-container-lib`). The main changes: - **Deleted** `lib/c/detect_cgroup_path.c` and `lib/c/detect_cgroup_path.h` - moved functionality into the new container library - **Added** `lib/c/gmt-container-lib.c` and `lib/c/gmt-container-lib.h` - new shared library containing: - `container_t` struct with `path`, `name`, `id`, and `pid` fields - `parse_containers()` function for parsing container IDs and resolving cgroup paths - `detect_cgroup_path()` for finding cgroup paths across different system configurations - `get_container_name()` using libcurl to query Docker API for container names - **Extended** `lib/c/gmt-lib.h` with `check_path()` function for system checks - **Refactored** all container-based metric providers to use the new shared library instead of duplicated local implementations - **Updated** all Makefiles to link against `gmt-container-lib.o` and `-lcurl` - **Added** libcurl dependency in `install_linux.sh` - **Added** test for early container exit behavior with container name in error messages Key benefits: eliminates ~400 lines of duplicated code, improves error messages by including container names, and creates a consistent API across providers.

title: Clearer container limit info
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors container information display by introducing a dedicated "Containers" tab and renaming `usage_scenario_dependencies` to `container_dependencies` for better clarity. The changes include database schema updates through migrations, frontend UI reorganization with a new tab, and backend data storage modifications. The refactoring separates container metadata (ID, name, CPU/memory limits) from dependency information, improving the user experience by organizing related information in dedicated UI sections. The changes span across database schema, scenario runner logic, frontend display components, and test files to maintain consistency. **Critical Issues Found:** - **XSS Vulnerability**: Frontend code inserts container data into HTML without proper escaping, creating a security vulnerability where malicious container data could execute arbitrary JavaScript - **Logic Error**: Arithmetic operations on `mem_limit` field that can be either a string ("1G") or integer (bytes), potentially resulting in `NaN` values when displaying memory information - **Unit Display Mismatch**: Code converts bytes to MB while displaying "MB" label, but the conversion formula suggests GB calculation **Confidence Score: 2/5** - While the refactoring improves code organization, the critical security vulnerability and logic errors require immediate attention before merging.

title: No backfilling of usage scenario. Rather using internal copy and freezing original
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors usage scenario handling by maintaining an immutable frozen copy (`_usage_scenario_original`) for storage while using a separate internal working copy (`__usage_scenario`) for runtime modifications. The containers data structure is also changed from an array to a dictionary (keyed by container name) for more efficient lookups. **Major Changes:** - Introduced `FrozenDict` class and `freeze_dict()` function to create immutable copies of the usage scenario - Split usage scenario into `_usage_scenario_original` (frozen, stored in DB) and `__usage_scenario` (mutable, used internally) - Changed containers storage format from array to dictionary for better performance - Updated frontend, tests, and optimization providers to work with new dict-based container structure **Issues Found:** - Test file treats containers as list when it's actually stored as dict (line 55-56 in `tests/test_resource_limits.py`) - Schema checker incorrectly validates the original copy instead of the working copy, potentially modifying data that should remain pristine (line 526 in `lib/scenario_runner.py`) - Error messages in duplicated `FrozenDict` class reference "GlobalConfig" instead of generic "FrozenDict" (lines 15-29 in `lib/utils.py`)

title: Reworked resource limits
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors resource limit handling by centralizing CPU and memory reservation logic into a new `lib/resource_limits.py` module. The changes ensure that GMT always reserves at least 1 CPU core for metric providers and allows configurable memory reservations to prevent OOM situations. **Key Changes:** - Created centralized `resource_limits.py` module with `get_assignable_cpus()` and `get_assignable_memory()` functions - Added mandatory `host_reserved_cpus` (min: 1) and `host_reserved_memory` configuration options - Enhanced system checks to validate resource availability before runs - Improved optimization provider messages with better criticality levels (added `GOOD` level) - Fixed memory utilization check to compare usage percentage instead of absolute values - Updated cpuset assignment logic to properly reserve CPUs for GMT **Overall Assessment:** The refactoring addresses the issues raised in previous review threads. The validation logic at `resource_limits.py:22-23` ensures `host_reserved_cpus >= 1`, and the cpuset calculation correctly generates CPU assignments. The code includes comprehensive system checks and proper error handling for resource constraints.

title: More containers info
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Adds additional container configuration information (CPUSet, Memory Swap, Memory Swappiness, OOM Score Adj.) to both the database storage and frontend display. **Key Changes:** - Backend now stores `cpuset`, `memory_swap`, `memory_swappiness`, and `oom_score_adj` in the containers data structure - Frontend displays these new fields with proper formatting (MB conversion for memory swap) - Refactored Docker run string construction to use `container_data` dict for consistency **Critical Issue:** - `oom_score_adj` is set to 0 instead of 1000, changing OOM behavior from "kill containers first" to "neutral priority"

title: (test-fix): Re-factored metric provider tests to reduce test flakyness
body:
- Skipped tests pytest natively for macOS - Calculated max factor according to used CPUs - Split up Memory and CPU test as Virtual Mem test has slower ramp-up time for CPU

Greptile Summary

Refactored metric provider tests to reduce flakiness by splitting CPU and memory stress tests and calculating CPU utilization factor based on available CPUs. Major changes: - Split VM Stress phase into separate Memory (006) and CPU (007) stress phases to handle different ramp-up times - Introduced `max_utilization_factor` calculation using `resource_limits.get_assignable_cpus() / os.cpu_count()` to scale CPU utilization assertions based on available CPUs - Converted inline macOS checks to `@pytest.mark.skipif` decorators for cleaner test skipping - Renamed `test_cpu_memory_carbon_providers` to `test_cpu_time_carbon_providers` and extracted memory tests to `test_memory_providers` - Applied `max_utilization_factor` to CPU utilization assertions for more realistic expectations on systems with limited CPU allocation Issues found: - Typo in assertion message on line 222 - Potential logic issue with macOS CPU utilization upper bound not being scaled by `max_utilization_factor`

title: Geo and carbon backfill
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR refactors geo-location and carbon intensity data handling by moving from inline API calls during data insertion to a backfill-based approach using cron jobs. ## Key Changes - Renamed columns: `ci_measurements.lat`/`lon` → `latitude`/`longitude` (text → double precision), `hog_simplified_measurements.grid_intensity_cog` → `carbon_intensity_g` - Removed geo-location and carbon intensity API calls from `api_helpers.py:carbondb_add` function - data now backfilled asynchronously - Added two new cron scripts: `backfill_geo.py` and `backfill_carbon_intensity.py` for populating missing data - Restructured `ip_data` table to use normalized columns instead of JSONB - Moved cache utility class to new `lib/cache_definitions.py` ## Issues Found - **CRITICAL**: Migration attempts to add `ip_address`, `latitude`, `longitude` columns to `carbondb_data_raw` that already exist in base schema, causing SQL error - Migration doesn't set `NOT NULL` constraints on `ip_address` for `ci_measurements` and `hog_simplified_measurements` tables (required by structure.sql) - Minor indentation issue in error logging - Inconsistent empty string handling for latitude/longitude validation

title: add missing disk type NVME for containers
body:
I've used GMT mostly on a Mac, where it is pretty limited, but now I've added a dual boot with Ubuntu/Linux so I can use GMT with Linux.

I tried running it with projects I tried before on your cluster, and got this error, originating from this file:

Partion inside a docker container found. This should not happen: 259:5 rbytes=247291904 wbytes=495616

With some research I found out that this 259 is a legit 'storage type' for NVMe's, so GMT shouldn't crash on that, and include the NVMe data in the metrics. For the rest, I don't know an awful lot about this, but I did realize that you can only run into this issue if you run this hardware, so I figured I add this patch, which did solve the run failure.

title: Better disk detection
body:
Greptile Overview

### Greptile Summary Enhanced disk device detection by adding support for NVMe devices (major 259) and additional device mapper ranges (251-254), plus added `lspci` and `lsblk` commands to hardware info collection for better debugging. - Added documentation for NVMe (259) and network block devices (43) major numbers - Expanded device mapper exclusion from just 254 to range 251-254 - Updated comments to clarify that major 8 is SCSI/SATA, not NVMe - Added comprehensive guideline comments explaining disk detection philosophy - Added `lspci` and `lsblk` to hardware info for better system visibility - Detection of partition moved from *minor % 16* approach to sysfs backed detection

Greptile Summary

Enhanced disk device detection by migrating from modulo-based partition detection to sysfs-based detection (`is_partition_sysfs`), which properly handles NVMe devices and other modern storage types. Extended device exclusion list to cover device mappers 251-254 and added comprehensive documentation for major/minor device numbers. - Added `is_partition_sysfs()` function in `lib/c/gmt-lib.c` that checks `/sys/dev/block/%u:%u/partition` for reliable partition detection across all device types - Replaced unreliable `minor_number % 16 != 0` partition check with sysfs-based detection in both procfs and cgroup implementations - Expanded device mapper exclusion from just 254 to range 251-254 - Added NVMe (259) and network block device (43) documentation - Added `lspci` and `lsblk` commands to hardware info for better system debugging

body:
Bumps [scipy](https://github.com/scipy/scipy) from 1.16.3 to 1.17.0.
Release notes

Sourced from scipy's releases.

SciPy 1.17.0 Release Notes

SciPy 1.17.0 is the culmination of 6 months of hard work. It contains many new features, numerous bug-fixes, improved test coverage and better documentation. There have been a number of deprecations and API changes in this release, which are documented below. All users are encouraged to upgrade to this release, as there are a large number of bug-fixes and optimizations. Before upgrading, we recommend that users check that their own code does not use deprecated SciPy functionality (to do so, run your code with python -Wd and check for DeprecationWarning s). Our development attention will now shift to bug-fix releases on the 1.17.x branch, and on adding new features on the main branch.

This release requires Python 3.11-3.14 and NumPy 1.26.4 or greater.

Highlights of this release

  • Many SciPy functions have gained native support for batching of N-dimensional array input and additional support for the array API standard. An overall summary of the latter is now available in a set of tables.
  • In scipy.sparse, coo_array now supports indexing. This includes integers, slices, arrays, np.newaxis, Ellipsis, in 1D, 2D and the relatively new nD. In scipy.sparse.linalg, ARPACK and PROPACK rewrites from Fortran77 to C now empower the use of external pseudorandom number generators, e.g. from numpy.
  • In scipy.spatial, transform.Rotation and transform.RigidTransform have been extended to support N-D arrays. geometric_slerp now has support for extrapolation.
  • scipy.stats has gained the matrix t and logistic distributions and many performance and accuracy improvements.
  • Initial support for 64-bit integer (ILP64) BLAS and LAPACK libraries has been added, including for MKL and Apple Accelerate. Please report any issues with ILP64 you encounter.

New features

scipy.integrate improvements

  • The integration routines dopri5, dopri853, LSODA, vode, and zvode have been ported from Fortran77 to C.
  • scipy.integrate.quad now has a fast path for returning 0 when the integration interval is empty.
  • The BDF, DOP853, RK23, RK45, OdeSolver, DenseOutput, ode, and complex_ode classes now support subscription, making them generic types, for compatibility with scipy-stubs.

title: Showing runs from other users also
body:
This PR integrates a long wished feature: Being able to see runs from other users also if they are visible. GMT internally has different understandings of what a "visible" run means. - Runs can be public. This means they are visible to everyone - A user can be visible. This is a functionality for bigger teams who have multiple users and want their runs generally to be hidden but visible inside a certain group of people. This PR brings the functionality to: - Always show runs by other visible users if you are the DEFAULT users - Only show runs by your user if you are a logged-in user - Have the option to toggle this behaviour off/on in the search - Setting will be saved in localStorage (until you clear your cookies) To have this working correctly on the cluster the same users that are visible to the DEFAULT user shoud be added to the visibility list of all non-public users

Greptile Overview

### Greptile Summary This PR adds functionality to control the visibility of runs from other users through a new `show_other_users` filter. The implementation includes both backend API support and frontend UI controls. ## Key Changes **Backend (api/scenario_runner.py)** - Added `show_other_users` parameter to `/v2/runs` endpoint - When `False`, filters to show only the current user's runs (`r.user_id = %s`) - When `True` or `None`, uses the existing visibility logic (super user, visible users, or public runs) **Frontend (frontend/js/helpers/runs.js)** - Extended `getFilterQueryStringFromURI()` to handle `show_other_users` parameter from URL params or localStorage - Modified `getFilterQueryStringFromInputs()` to include `show_other_users` in form submissions - Settings are persisted in localStorage with defaults: `'true'` for DEFAULT user, `'false'` for logged-in users **Authentication (frontend/js/authentication.js)** - Sets `show_other_users` to `'false'` in localStorage when a user logs in, ensuring logged-in users only see their own runs by default **UI (frontend/runs.html)** - Added radio button controls for the "Show runs from other users" setting - Marked with a save icon to indicate the setting persists across reloads ## Issues Found Several logic and consistency issues were identified: 1. **Critical**: The `/v1/repositories` endpoint doesn't support `show_other_users` filtering, but the frontend calls it with this parameter. This causes repositories to always show all visible users, but when expanded, the nested runs respect the filter, leading to confusing empty results. 2. **Critical**: When expanding a repository accordion, duplicate `uri` parameters are sent to the API if there's a `uri` in the URL params, causing the wrong URI to be filtered. 3. **Important**: The clear button doesn't preserve `show_archived` and `show_other_users` settings from localStorage, resetting them to defaults instead of respecting user preferences. 4. **Minor**: Redundant DOM query on line 153 of runs.js 5. **Minor**: Storing `undefined` as string in localStorage when no radio is checked The core functionality is sound, but these issues need to be addressed for consistent behavior across the application.

title: Email templates
body:
This PR introduces an email templating system that can be used to send styled and custom emails depending on the action. It has two general categories: - Simple emails - Here just a text message is sent as plain text - Report emails - Will be sent as HTML Multipart - Load a txt and a html template that can contain dynamic vars to replace The way to decide when to use a template and which is based on the "category" of a run. Currently only two categories are known: - Websites - General Both rendered templates attached as example

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a comprehensive email templating system for sending styled HTML emails with dynamic variable replacement. The implementation adds email job types (`email-simple` and `email-report`), template files for website and general categories, and database schema changes to support category-based template selection.

Changes Overview

- **Email Infrastructure**: New email job classes (`EmailSimpleJob`, `EmailReportJob`) that extend an abstract `EmailJob` base class - **Template System**: Added 4 email templates (2 text + 2 HTML) for website and general categories with variable placeholders - **Database Schema**: Renamed `categories` column to `category_ids` across `runs`, `jobs`, and `watchlist` tables; added validation triggers to enforce referential integrity - **Integration**: Updated API, cron, and runner modules to pass category IDs through the job system

Key Implementation Details

- Templates use mustache-style placeholders like `{{__GMT_RUN_ID__}}` that are replaced at send time - Category selection is based on presence of "Websites" category name, determining which template set is used - Database migration creates triggers that validate category array elements exist in the `categories` reference table - Error emails now use the new email-simple job type

Issues Identified

1. **Missing Error Handling for Template Files** (line 92-95 in `lib/job/email_report.py`): Template files are opened without try-except, so missing templates will produce generic `FileNotFoundError` messages without context about which file failed.

title: Encoding errors
body:
Greptile Summary

Adds `encoding='UTF-8', errors='replace'` parameters to subprocess calls throughout the codebase to handle encoding errors gracefully. This prevents potential `UnicodeDecodeError` exceptions when subprocess output contains invalid UTF-8 sequences. Key changes: - Replaces `text=True` with explicit `encoding='UTF-8', errors='replace'` in subprocess calls - Adds encoding parameters to `subprocess.check_output()` calls that previously lacked them - Covers main application code in lib/, metric_providers/, cron/, and tools/ The `errors='replace'` parameter ensures that invalid UTF-8 sequences are replaced with the Unicode replacement character (�) instead of raising exceptions, improving robustness when dealing with potentially malformed output from external commands.

title: Acl volume loading
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Replaces the `allow_unsafe` capability with a more granular `allowed_volume_mounts` list that allows administrators to whitelist specific volumes (with read/write permissions) that users can mount. Changes volume mounting from using `-v` flags to the more explicit and secure `--mount` syntax with comma validation to prevent injection attacks. Key changes: - Database migration removes `allow_unsafe` and adds `allowed_volume_mounts` array to user capabilities - Volume mounts are validated against an allow-list that includes both source and mount option (e.g., `volume-name,readonly`) - All internal mounts (repo, relations, playwright) converted to `--mount` syntax with comma validation - Writeable mounts are now supported for both allow-listed and safe-path volumes - Non-allowed volumes are restricted to paths within the working folder (using existing `_join_paths` protection) **Issues found:** - Security: Missing comma validation for `mount_target` in allowed volume/bind mount paths (lines 1293, 1299) - users could inject additional mount options - Migration inconsistency: System user (id=0) has `allow_unsafe` removed but doesn't get `allowed_volume_mounts` added ## Summary This pull request refactors volume mounting security in the metrics tool by replacing the blanket `allow_unsafe` capability with a more granular `allowed_volume_mounts` allow-list, and updates Docker mounting syntax from `-v` flags to `--mount` with comma validation. ### Key Changes **Security & Volume Handling:** - Removes `allow_unsafe` capability; replaces with `allowed_volume_mounts` array in user capabilities (example: `"volume-name,readonly"`) - Switches Docker volume mounting from `-v` syntax to `--mount` syntax with comma validation to prevent mount option injection - Validates volumes against allow-list; non-allowed volumes restricted to working folder paths via existing `_join_paths` protection - Supports writeable mounts for both allow-listed and safe-path volumes - For allow-listed volumes without `/`, treats as named Docker volume; otherwise treats as host path **CLI & Configuration Flags (Renamed):** - `--skip-system-checks` → `--dev-no-system-checks` - `--dev-no-optimizations` → `--skip-optimizations` (affecting optimization reporter gating) - Reorganized CLI argument sections: system-check options now labeled as development flags **Database:** - Migration `2026_01_26_volume_mounts.sql` removes `measurement.allow_unsafe` and adds `measurement.allowed_volume_mounts: []` for all users except system user (id=0) - Updated seeded defaults in `structure.sql` to reflect new capabilities structure **Code Updates:** - `ScenarioRunner.__init__`: removed `skip_system_checks` and `dev_no_optimizations` parameters; added `dev_no_system_checks` and `allowed_volume_mounts` - Updated volume inspection in `_save_image_and_volume_sizes` to no longer depend on `allow_unsafe` flag - Refactored internal mounts (repo, relations, Playwright IPC) to use `--mount` with path validation **Frontend/UI:** - Updated settings HTML and JavaScript to reflect `skip_optimizations` checkbox instead of `dev_no_optimizations` - Added frontend test coverage for the new optimization flag **Tests:** - Updated 15+ test files to use new `dev_no_system_checks` and `skip_optimizations` parameters - Added named volume tests: `test_allowed_volume_should_work`, `test_allowed_volume_readonly_works`, `test_non_permitted_volume_should_fail`, `test_allowed_volume_fails_bc_readonly` - Added readonly scenario file `volume_load_non_bind_mounts_readonly.yml` ### Known Issues (from PR discussion) - Missing comma validation for mount_target in allowed volume/bind mount paths (lines 1293, 1299) — potential injection vulnerability - Migration inconsistency: system user (id=0) has `allow_unsafe` removed but does not receive `allowed_volume_mounts` initialization - Author noted writeable mounts may need reversal to readonly if unresolved security concerns emerge around symlink resolution

  • Fix forwarded_allow_ips and proxy_allow_ips to remain as strings for backward compatibility with external tools like uvicorn. Network validation now uses strict mode to detect invalid CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.1.1/24 where host bits are set) (#3458, [PR #3459](benoitc/gunicorn#3459))

Gunicorn 24.1.0

New Features

  • Official Docker Image: Gunicorn now publishes official Docker images to GitHub Container Registry ([PR #3454](benoitc/gunicorn#3454))

    • Available at ghcr.io/benoitc/gunicorn
    • Based on Python 3.12 slim image
    • Uses recommended worker formula (2 × CPU + 1)
    • Configurable via environment variables

  • PROXY Protocol v2 Support: Extended PROXY protocol implementation to support the binary v2 format in addition to the existing text-based v1 format ([PR #3451](benoitc/gunicorn#3451))

    • New --proxy-protocol modes: off, v1, v2, auto
    • auto mode (default when enabled) detects v1 or v2 automatically
    • v2 binary format is more efficient and supports additional metadata
    • Works with HAProxy, AWS NLB/ALB, and other PROXY protocol v2 sources

  • CIDR Network Support: --forwarded-allow-ips and --proxy-allow-from now accept CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.0.0/16) for specifying trusted networks ([PR #3449](benoitc/gunicorn#3449))

  • Socket Backlog Metric: New gunicorn.socket.backlog gauge metric reports the current socket backlog size on Linux systems ([PR #3450](benoitc/gunicorn#3450))

  • InotifyReloader Enhancement: The inotify-based reloader now watches newly imported modules, not just those loaded at startup ([PR #3447](benoitc/gunicorn#3447))

Bug Fixes

  • Fix signal handling regression where SIGCLD alias caused "Unhandled signal: cld" errors on Linux when workers fail during boot (#3453)
  • Fix socket blocking mode on keepalive connections preventing SSL handshake failures with async workers ([PR #3452](benoitc/gunicorn#3452))
  • Use smaller buffer size in finish_body() for faster timeout detection on slow or abandoned connections ([PR #3453](benoitc/gunicorn#3453))
  • Handle SSLWantReadError in finish_body() to prevent worker hangs during SSL renegotiation ([PR #3448](benoitc/gunicorn#3448))
  • Log SIGTERM as info level instead of warning to reduce noise in orchestrated environments ([PR #3446](benoitc/gunicorn#3446))
  • Print exception details to stderr when worker fails to boot ([PR #3443](benoitc/gunicorn#3443))
  • Fix unreader.unread() to prepend data to buffer instead of appending ([PR #3442](benoitc/gunicorn#3442))
  • Prevent RecursionError when pickling Config objects ([PR #3441](benoitc/gunicorn#3441))
  • Use proper exception chaining with raise from in glogging.py ([PR #3440](benoitc/gunicorn#3440))

title: (fix): Hardware Info Root Sudoers entry was possible to hijack
body:
This PR addresses a security vulnerability in the sudoers entries that GMT creates. The module resolution for `-m lib.hardware_info_root` could b hijacked by creating a malicious directory *lib* somewhere and placing an alternative *hardware_info_root* in it. The fix moves all necessary root executable files to /usr/local/bin/green-metrics-tool Futhermore the checking mechanism was updated to fully resolve any symlinks and further hardened by checking and failing if ACLs are present. ## How to update Just run the GMT install script again as you would normally when updating. It will overwrite the old vulnerable sudoers entry ## How to find out if your system has been exploited Search for `find / 2>/dev/null | grep hardware_info_root` If a hardware_info_root.py turns up that is not in the GMT directory at the expected location (*lib/hardware_info_root.py*) you should investigate ## Impact We know of no use of this vulnerability. It can only be exploited if a user already has access to the host the GMT is running on. However it elevates priviledges and thus should be considered high severity.

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR hardens the sudoers entries created by GMT by switching privileged helper invocations (e.g., `hardware_info_root.py`, `maintenance.py`, `sysctl`, `ipmi-dcmi`, `powermetrics`) to absolute paths and adding a recursive ownership/permission/ACL check (`check_file_permissions`) to reduce path/module hijacking risk. Runtime code paths were updated to call `/usr/local/bin/green-metrics-tool/{hardware_info_root.py,maintenance.py}` with a fully-resolved `/usr/bin/python3`. Main issue found: the new “disable path security checks” switch is wired inconsistently. `lib/install_shared.sh` parses `--disable-path-security`, but CI and devcontainer scripts pass `--disable_path_security_checks`, so those environments won’t actually disable the checks and may fail installs after this change. Align the flag name between the parser and the call sites.

title: Bump gunicorn from 23.0.0 to 25.0.0
body:
Bumps [gunicorn](https://github.com/benoitc/gunicorn) from 23.0.0 to 25.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from gunicorn's releases.

Gunicorn 25.0.0

New Features

  • Dirty Arbiters: Separate process pool for executing long-running, blocking operations (AI model loading, heavy computation) without blocking HTTP workers ([PR #3460](benoitc/gunicorn#3460))

    • Inspired by Erlang's dirty schedulers
    • Asyncio-based with Unix socket IPC
    • Stateful workers that persist loaded resources
    • New settings: --dirty-app, --dirty-workers, --dirty-timeout, --dirty-threads, --dirty-graceful-timeout
    • Lifecycle hooks: on_dirty_starting, dirty_post_fork, dirty_worker_init, dirty_worker_exit

  • Per-App Worker Allocation for Dirty Arbiters: Control how many dirty workers load each app for memory optimization with heavy models ([PR #3473](benoitc/gunicorn#3473))

    • Set workers class attribute on DirtyApp (e.g., workers = 2)
    • Or use config format module:class:N (e.g., myapp:HeavyModel:2)
    • Requests automatically routed to workers with the target app
    • New exception DirtyNoWorkersAvailableError for graceful error handling
    • Example: 8 workers × 10GB model = 80GB → with workers=2: 20GB (75% savings)

  • HTTP/2 Support (Beta): Native HTTP/2 (RFC 7540) support for improved performance with modern clients ([PR #3468](benoitc/gunicorn#3468))

    • Multiplexed streams over a single connection
    • Header compression (HPACK)
    • Flow control and stream prioritization
    • Works with gthread, gevent, and ASGI workers
    • New settings: --http-protocols, --http2-max-concurrent-streams, --http2-initial-window-size, --http2-max-frame-size, --http2-max-header-list-size
    • Requires SSL/TLS and h2 library: pip install gunicorn[http2]
    • New example: examples/http2_gevent/ with Docker and tests

  • HTTP 103 Early Hints: Support for RFC 8297 Early Hints to enable browsers to preload resources before the final response ([PR #3468](benoitc/gunicorn#3468))

    • WSGI: environ['wsgi.early_hints'](https://github.com/benoitc/gunicorn/blob/HEAD/headers) callback
    • ASGI: http.response.informational message type
    • Works with both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2

  • uWSGI Protocol for ASGI Worker: The ASGI worker now supports receiving requests via the uWSGI binary protocol from nginx ([PR #3467](benoitc/gunicorn#3467))

Bug Fixes

  • Fix HTTP/2 ALPN negotiation for gevent and eventlet workers when do_handshake_on_connect is False (the default). The TLS handshake is now explicitly performed before checking selected_alpn_protocol().

title: Streaming outputs
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a new `--dev-stream-outputs` flag that allows streaming output from container builds and flow/setup commands directly to the terminal, which is useful for debugging during local development. **Key changes:** - Removed deprecated `stream-stdout` and `stream-stderr` options from the schema (these were per-command flags) - Added global `--dev-stream-outputs` flag that controls streaming behavior across all operations - Updated schema validation to no longer check for conflicts with the removed streaming options **Issues found:** - **Critical**: Duplicate line assignment at line 1654 in `scenario_runner.py` - **Critical**: Multiple error handling paths (lines 1015, 1668-1670) will display "None" instead of actual error output when streaming is enabled, because `ps.stdout` and `ps.stderr` are `None` when `stdout=None` and `stderr=None` are passed to `subprocess.run()` - **Critical**: Process output handling at lines 2196-2197 will pass `None` values to `_handle_process_output()` when streaming is enabled The warning messages correctly inform users that streaming "disallows capturing of errors and build outputs," but the code still attempts to access `ps.stdout` and `ps.stderr` in error messages, which will be `None`.

title: Cache relations
body:
This PR allows for caching the relations folder and the checkout out repository. In order to allow this some refactorings where needed: - Moving most os. to Pathlib - Never clearing the folder on start. Rather modularizing the folders for metrics, repo and relations and clearing them separately - Injecting the path into the metric providers Further this introduces delete of the /tmp/green-metrics-tool folder on the cluster after every run

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

- Refactors temp-folder handling to split `/tmp/green-metrics-tool` into subfolders (`repo/`, `relations/`, `metrics/`, `docker_images/`) and injects the metrics folder into all metric providers. - Adds `--dev-cache-repos` to reuse already-cloned `repo` and `relations` directories across runs. - Removes the old utils-based “outside symlink” detection and replaces it with a Pathlib-based scan inside `ScenarioRunner`. - Adds cluster-side cleanup by deleting the tmp folder after `RunJob` completes, and keeps optional `--file-cleanup` deletion in CLI mode.

title: Added OS Package Update block in cluster mode
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Refactored cluster maintenance by renaming `cleanup.py` to `maintenance.py` and adding optional OS package updates via a new `--update-os-packages` flag. The flag is controlled by a config setting `cluster.client.update_os_packages` and only triggers once per 24 hours based on `/var/log/apt/history.log` modification time. Major changes: - Renamed `tools/cluster/cleanup_original.py` to `tools/cluster/maintenance_original.py` with refactored code structure (split into functions: `cleanup()`, `sync_ntp()`, `check_systemd_timers()`, `update_os_packages()`) - Added `--update-os-packages` argument to maintenance script - Updated `cron/client.py` to check config and file timestamp before passing flag - Modernized path handling using `pathlib.Path` instead of `os.path` - Updated `install_linux.sh` to reference new script name **Critical issues found:** - Config key path in `cron/client.py:75` is incorrect - should be `config['cluster']['client']['update_os_packages']` not `config['cluster']['update_os_packages']` - Empty string being passed to subprocess in `cron/client.py:84` will cause argparse errors - Path object needs string conversion for subprocess.run

title: Hardening the subit by making the file also unwriteable by group
body:
Technically not needed as the subit already pops when the file is modified anyway. But there is no need to have the file group writeable, so locking it down

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR hardens several setuid metric-provider build targets by changing the post-build ownership step from `sudo chown root $@` to `sudo chown root:root $@`, ensuring the resulting binaries are owned by group `root` rather than inheriting a potentially writable group. This fits into the codebase’s pattern of compiling small metric-provider binaries and then setting ownership/permissions (including setuid) so they can access privileged system interfaces at runtime. Issues found: - Several Makefiles now lack a trailing newline, producing `\ No newline at end of file` diffs and potentially tripping strict text-file checks.

title: Skip dev switches alignment
body:
This PR aligns the domains and intended effects of switches in GMT. --skip switches should not break or skew measurements. Also data that depends on other data should not be missing. Using them should only speed up the tool but do not have side effects --dev switches can break and skew measurements

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR reorganizes command-line flags to better communicate their effects on measurements. The key changes are: - Renamed `--skip-system-checks` to `--dev-no-system-checks` - moved to dev switches since skipping system checks can lead to skewed measurements - Renamed `--dev-no-optimizations` to `--skip-optimizations` - moved out of dev switches since skipping optimizations only affects post-processing, not measurement data itself The refactoring establishes clearer semantics: - `--skip-*` flags: safe to use, only skip optional post-processing or speed up runs without affecting measurement accuracy - `--dev-*` flags: intended for development only, may break or skew measurements All changes are applied consistently across the codebase including runner.py, ScenarioRunner, database schema, frontend, and all test files. The `.devcontainer/splash.md` file also fixes a pre-existing typo (`--dev-no-optimization` → `--skip-optimizations`).

title: Skip container dependency collection
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

Introduces `--dev-no-container-dependency-collection` flag to skip container dependency collection during development runs, speeding up testing. **Key changes:** - Added new `dev_no_container_dependency_collection` parameter to `ScenarioRunner` and updated all tests to use optimization flags consistently - Updated database schema to include the new flag in user ACLs and default settings - Modified `_collect_container_dependencies()` to check the flag and return early if set - Reorganized instance variable assignments in `ScenarioRunner.__init__()` for better grouping **Issues found:** - Typo in `runner.py` comment: "generateda" → "generated" - Duplicate `--skip-download-dependencies` flag in one test - Print statement order may cause misleading output when skipping dependency collection

title: docker compose compatibility
body:
When I have
```
services:
  web:
    build: .
    command: >-
      sh -c "python manage.py migrate &&
      python manage.py collectstatic --noinput &&
      python manage.py import_sample_data &&
      gunicorn todo_project.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"
    volumes:
      - .:/app
```
somehow the `"..."` are deleted so I get 
```
docker run -it ... sh -c python manage.py migrate && python manage.py collectstatic --noinput && python manage.py import_sample_data && gunicorn todo_project.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000
```
which is not the same as:
```
docker run -it ... sh -c "python manage.py migrate && python manage.py collectstatic --noinput && python manage.py import_sample_data && gunicorn todo_project.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"
```

when I call `docker compose up` everything is fine. When I use the GMT it fails.

title: small fixes
body: Fixes #1549

title: Compose file trip wire
body:
I have a compose file in a project. 

```
services:
  web:
    build: .
    volumes:
      - .:/app
```

which is fairly standard when developing. Everything works fine when I do `docker compose up` in my project dir. 

Now when I try to test the `usage_scenario.yml` docker is called with

```
docker run -it -d --name web -v .:/app ...
```
from the GMT which I have called with `--allow-unsafe` because I am developing. 

Now the program fails and it is not quite clear why. Looking at the problem it then makes sense, that the GMT dir is mapped into the container and not the project dir. I think we should warn or do something in this case as this is something I see happening quite frequently. Took me some time to debug.

title: Logical draft of how the metric processors shall work
body:
This PR outlines the concept of introducing two new stages to the GMT:

- Post Metric Processors
- Post Phases Stat Processors

They run in the pipeline as follows:
Metric Providers -> Post Metric Processors -> Phase Stats -> Post Phase Stats Processors

The already commited `config.yml.example` outlines how they are defined in the config.

## Simplifications and Domain Logic

This PR simplifies the mental load on where processing happens in the GMT and makes it more explicit and more modular.

- The `phase_stats.py` will then really only create avg and aggregate values of metric data
- SCI will not be all over the place but in a separate stage. Making it also more easy to get SCI values per phase
- Overloaded Providers like XGBoost and SDIA are then in their separate stage. Not having the need to be processed last in the metric provider stage and loading in "hopefully" generated values by other providers ... which is currently only by accident :)


## When we implement this approach the following refactorings need to be done:

- Rip out the `calculate_co2_intensity` from the `phase_stats.py` and bring it to a Post Metric Processor (https://github.com/green-coding-solutions/green-metrics-tool/blob/d0a621556f7e9c7b188b7dd43514b77106bbb04d/lib/phase_stats.py#L81)
- Migrate the XGBoost and SDIA providers to be Post Metric Processors
- Migrate the SCI generation code from the `phase_stats` and bring it to the Post Phases Stats Processors 
- Look at https://if.greensoftware.foundation/pipelines/ to see if we can take some good ideas from how IF thinks about pipelines. We want it less complex. But still might find some good work there

title: Further hardening
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR adds security hardening by using absolute paths for system commands, clearing environment variables, replacing argparse with manual argv parsing, and adding Python isolation flags (`-I`, `-B`, `-S`) to prevent site packages and user scripts from being loaded. Key changes: - Replaced `argparse` with manual `sys.argv` parsing since argparse depends on `os.environ` - Added `os.environ.clear()` to prevent environment variable injection - Changed all system commands to use absolute paths (e.g., `/usr/bin/sudo`, `/usr/bin/apt`) since `PATH` was cleared - Added Python flags `-I` (isolated mode), `-B` (no bytecode), `-S` (no site packages) to all sudo python invocations - Replaced `os.environ['SUDO_USER']` with a templated `__GMT_USER__` variable that gets replaced during installation Issues found: - In `maintenance_original.py:120`, the `env` parameter won't work as expected since `os.environ` was cleared at line 6 - The `sed` command at `install_linux.sh:94` needs `sudo` prefix since the file is in a root-owned directory

title: Carbondb timestamp fix
body:
Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes timestamp handling when copying Power HOG data to CarbonDB. The key changes are: - Fixed the `time` field calculation in `copy_over_power_hog()` to use the actual energy consumption timestamp instead of the database insertion time (`created_at`) - Changed from `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM created_at) * 1e6` to `"timestamp" * 1e3`, correctly converting milliseconds to microseconds since the `timestamp` field in `hog_simplified_measurements` is already in milliseconds - Updated all three copy functions to use `NOW()` for the `created_at` field in `carbondb_data_raw`, ensuring it reflects the actual insertion time into CarbonDB rather than the source table's creation time - Extended the validation window from 30 days to 31 days to prevent race conditions with the 30-day merge window

title: Mounting relations also in build stage
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR makes two related changes to Docker container configuration in `ScenarioRunner`: 1. **Mounts relations in the build stage**: Relations (external git repos cloned as dependencies) are now bind-mounted into the Kaniko build container at `/tmp/relations/{relation_key}`, matching the existing behavior in the run stage. This allows Dockerfiles to `COPY` or reference files from relation repos during `docker build`. 2. **Migrates run stage from `-v` to `--mount` syntax**: The repo mount, relation mounts, and Playwright IPC mount in the run stage are converted from Docker's `-v`/`--volume` shorthand to the more explicit `--mount` flag. This is a security hardening — `--mount` has stricter parsing (fails on typos instead of silently creating directories) and aligns the run stage with the build stage which already used `--mount`. - Comma validation is added defensively for `relation['mount_path']` in both build and run stages to prevent `--mount` parameter injection via the `,src=` directive. - Comma validation for `repo_mount_path` is newly added in the run stage (it was already present in the build stage). title: GMT can checkout repository and relations at defined commit hash
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds the ability to check out repositories and relations at a specific commit hash, extending both the CLI (`--commit-hash`) and web API/frontend. The implementation centralizes checkout logic in a new `_checkout_commit_hash` method that handles shallow clones gracefully by fetching specific commits when they're not in the shallow history. Database schema, job pipeline, and frontend are updated consistently. - **Bug in `SchemaChecker.is_valid_commit_hash`**: The method returns a boolean instead of raising `SchemaError` / returning the value. When used with `Use()` in the schema validation, this silently replaces the commit hash string with `True`/`False`, breaking relation checkout. This needs to be fixed before merge. - **No API-level format validation**: The `commit_hash` received from the web frontend/API is stored directly in the jobs table without format validation. Invalid values will only fail asynchronously when the job runs, giving users poor feedback. - Good test coverage with two new tests covering both main repository and relation commit hash checkout. - The symlink check ordering (previously discussed) is now correct for both the main repository and relations paths. Last reviewed commit: d97545f

title: Usage scenario variables as array
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR refactors how usage scenario variables are passed between the frontend and backend, moving from JSON-encoded strings to URL array syntax (`usage_scenario_variables[KEY]=VALUE`). The backend now uses a FastAPI dependency (`parse_usage_scenario_variables`) to parse these from the query string, and `get_timeline_query` builds parameterized SQL conditions for each key-value pair. The frontend replaces the single text input with a dynamic key-value form with add/remove functionality and a "no variables" checkbox. The overall approach is sound — array-style query params are more standard for key-value data than JSON-in-URL, and the new form UI is more user-friendly. Key observations: - The backend correctly uses parameterized queries (`%s` placeholders with `params.extend`) to prevent SQL injection when building per-key conditions. - The `Annotated[..., Depends(...)]` pattern is the correct modern FastAPI approach for custom parameter parsing. - Bracket encoding (`[`/`]` → `%5B`/`%5D`) round-trips correctly through both JavaScript `URLSearchParams` and Python Starlette's `QueryParams`. - `buildQueryParams()` can now throw (due to form validation), but is called outside try-catch blocks in `loadCharts`, which could cause unhandled errors. - `getUsageScenarioVariablesFromForm()` is called redundantly multiple times per chart load. Last reviewed commit: 38bccda

title: Not using Posix splitting as we often do have literal strings in commands
body:
We are seeing very often very complex commands sent to GMT that can include literal strings and also block text. Thus shlex.split is too restrictive here when used in POSIX mode. This fixes shlex.split to use relaxed non POSIX mode for issuing flow commands, setup-commands and also container run commands. The fix should have no security implication as escaping is still done by subprocess. An example command that failed before with the error "No closing quotation": `bash run-template.sh ai 'Trouver une solution pour refroidir processeurs à la place de l\"eau ' --dev-no-sleeps --dev-no-system-checks --dev-no-save` This should however work as we want to give the literal string to the AI model. it is not a series of CLI commands

Greptile Summary

This PR changes `shlex.split()` to use non-POSIX mode (`posix=False`) in three locations where commands are parsed: container run commands, setup commands, and flow commands. The change relaxes quote handling to support literal strings with unmatched or escaped quotes, like the example with French text containing `\"`. Since the parsed commands are still passed as lists to `subprocess.run()` and `subprocess.Popen()`, the security boundary remains intact - subprocess still handles proper escaping and prevents shell injection. **Key observations:** - Affects command parsing for `service['command']`, setup commands, and flow commands - All three locations pass parsed commands as lists to subprocess functions, maintaining security - The change is backward compatible for most well-formed commands - Solves the "No closing quotation" error for complex literal strings Last reviewed commit: 71338af

title: Compare Mode still allowed without settings if only two IDs encountered. Still warning is displayed
body:
When only two IDs are compared the current comparison still can trigger an error. This is because more than two attributes differ (URI, branch, commit_hash etc.) Since same and differing attributes can not easily selected and also comparison is harder when more than one attribute changed so far the mode failed. Since our opinion on this changed and we rather want to display something with a warning than nothing at all, this PR implements exactly that. A "minimal additional info" mode called "IDs" is now introduced which shows no additional info in the top info box. But also shows a warning that this comparison is to be made with caution.

Greptile Summary

Introduces a fallback "IDs" comparison mode that allows comparing two runs even when multiple attributes differ (repository, branch, commit hash, etc.), displaying a warning instead of failing. This improves user experience by showing comparisons with appropriate caveats rather than blocking them entirely. Key changes: - Wrapped the comparison case detection logic in a try-catch block in `api_helpers.py` - Falls back to 'IDs' mode when exactly 2 IDs are provided but don't match any standard comparison case - Added warning message in the frontend to inform users about the limitations of IDs mode comparison - Updated key selection logic to use `run_id` for the IDs case (same as single view mode) Last reviewed commit: 51f24e7

title: Checks in DB for carbon intensity if >= 0
body:
Greptile Summary

Adds database constraints to ensure `carbon_intensity_g` values are positive across three tables (`ci_measurements`, `hog_simplified_measurements`, `carbondb_data_raw`). **Critical Issues:** - PR title says ">= 0" but code implements "> 0" - excluding zero carbon intensity (possible with 100% renewable energy) - Type casting inconsistency: `int` columns compared to `0::double precision` instead of plain `0` - Migration and `structure.sql` have different constraint syntax (with/without type cast) - Migration lacks named constraints, making them harder to manage **Notes:** - Updated comment in `carbondb_data_raw` from "not null as it might contain errors" to "nullable as we want to backfill missing data" (correct clarification) Last reviewed commit: 4587074

title: Time series notes history
body:
To compare runs by their timing steps this PR introduces a chart that displays deltas and cumulative time.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a new "Time Series Notes History" chart to the compare view that visualizes timing deltas between two runs using cumulative time lines and candlestick charts. **Key changes:** - Modified `/v1/notes/{run_id}` API to calculate duration between consecutive notes using SQL `LEAD` window function - Added new chart section in `compare.html` with loader and error states - Implemented `fetchAndShowTimeSeriesNotesHistory()` function to fetch notes for two runs and render the comparison chart - Refactored variable names from `url_params['id']` to `run_id` and `url_params['ids']` to `run_ids` throughout `stats.js` and `compare.js` for better clarity - Upgraded Apache ECharts library (to support candlestick charts) - Moved `fetchTimelineNotes()` helper function from `stats.js` to `main.js` for reuse **Issues found:** - Missing null check before calling `.map()` on notes data (will crash if API returns null) - Missing `const` keyword for `option` variable (creates global variable) - SQL ordering changed from `DESC` to `ASC` which changes API behavior Last reviewed commit: 27816ed

title: Added /v2/timeline endpoint to get usage_scenario_variables in request and render in timeline
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a `/v2/timeline` API endpoint that extends the existing `/v1/timeline` (now deprecated) by including `usage_scenario_variables` in each returned run record. The frontend is updated to consume this new endpoint, sourcing per-run variable data directly from the API response instead of reading from a global filter widget. **Key changes:** - `get_timeline_query` gains a `v2` flag that conditionally adds `r.usage_scenario_variables` to the SQL `SELECT` clause. - A new `/v2/timeline` FastAPI route mirrors `/v1/timeline` exactly, passing `v2=True`. - `/v2/timeline` is added to the allowed routes in `structure.sql`. - The frontend destructures the new column and displays per-run `usage_scenario_variables` in the chart tooltip. **Issues found:** - A `console.log(data)` debug statement was left in `frontend/js/timeline.js` at line 344 and must be removed before merging. - The tooltip formatter now interpolates `stringifyUsageScenarioVariables()` output directly into `container.innerHTML` without the `escapeString()` wrapper that was present in the previous implementation. This removes a critical security safeguard: HTML special characters (or intentionally crafted markup) stored in a run's `usage_scenario_variables` can now be rendered as executable HTML, introducing an XSS vulnerability. Last reviewed commit: 9c622b1 > Greptile also left **1 inline comment** on this PR.

title: Notes can now be compared even with unequal text
body:
Notes are now allowed to differ slightly in text, which can happen if dynamic text is present in notes In that case a warning line is shown. This features is needed as we want to allow dynamic note texts and only fail if amount is not identical.

Greptile Summary

This PR updates the Time Series Notes comparison feature to allow notes with slightly different text to still be compared, showing a warning when notes differ in text. The chart renders with dual x-axes (one per run) to accommodate per-step label differences. **Issues found:** - **`dataZoom` desync (logic):** The slider's `xAxisIndex` is `0`, controlling only Run 1's axis and the Step Delta series. Run 2 (`xAxisIndex: 1`) is not controlled by the zoom, causing visual misalignment when zooming. - **Inconsistent `differences` return type (style):** `arraysCompare` returns a `string` for the length-mismatch case and an `array` for all other cases, making the function harder to reason about and fragile to future refactoring.

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `frontend/js/compare.js`, line 197-204 ([link](https://github.com/green-coding-solutions/green-metrics-tool/blob/a35a408097542406b56d694acc53162c8df4ed0d/frontend/js/compare.js#L197-L204)) `dataZoom` does not sync the second x-axis The slider uses `xAxisIndex: 0`, which only controls the x-axis for Run 1. Run 2 is plotted with `xAxisIndex: 1` (line 251), so when the user drags the zoom slider, Run 1 and Step Delta will zoom while Run 2 remains unzoomed, causing visual misalignment. title: Added one-shot option to MCP power reading script
body:
This PR has no direct functional value for the GMT, but enables the MCP power reading script to "one-shot". We need this often when doing power tests on machines, where we re-use the modular metric providers. Additionaly to the one-shot mode it also enables to use the MCP in energy accumulation mode instead of just using it to get the current effective power. This is needed to use it as a drop in replacement to the RAPL energy counter interface in intel processors

Greptile Summary

This PR extends the MCP power reading script with a one-shot mode (`-o`), energy accumulation mode (`-e`), and a range register dump (`-x`), enabling the tool to function as a drop-in replacement for RAPL energy counters. New helper functions (`f511_get_energy`, `f511_set_energy_counting`, `parse_le32`, `parse_le64`) are well-structured, and the `.h` header is correctly updated with missing includes and a trailing newline. Key issues found: - **Copy-paste bug in `f511_dump_range_registers` (line 330):** `Current2` is printed using `range1` instead of `range2`, so both channels always display the Channel 1 current range value — the Channel 2 current field is never shown. - **Hardcoded range register check runs unconditionally (lines 335–369, 465):** `f511_check_range_registers` hard-exits if range registers don't exactly match values 18/12/19. Since this runs on every invocation (including `oneshot` and `energy_mode`), any MCP device with different calibration values will fail before producing a single measurement — potentially at odds with the stated portability goal. - **Redundant duplicate `0x4E`/`0x4e` in `expected_len` condition (lines 154–158):** The two hex literals are identical in value; one is dead code and should be removed to avoid confusion with the `wait_ack` check below which only lists the value once. Last reviewed commit: ["REmoved duplicate if..."](https://github.com/green-coding-solutions/green-metrics-tool/commit/5a1a4239fd512743c4e6ec71d46eb105b9cc978d) > Greptile also left **2 inline comments** on this PR.

title: Changelog in timeline
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds cluster changelog entries as vertical mark lines on the timeline charts, allowing users to see infrastructure/machine changes in context with measurement data. It also refactors `calculateStatistics` to handle multiple data shapes without a boolean flag, fixes the stddev series lookup to use `find()` instead of a hardcoded index (making it robust when extra series like the changelog series are inserted), and changes the default sort order from "Date of commit" to "Date of measurement". Key changes: - **`api/main.py`**: Extends `/v1/cluster/changelog` with `start_date`, `end_date`, and `show_package_updates` filters. The `machine_id` condition is broadened to also include entries where `machine_id IS NULL` (machine-agnostic entries). Note: `end_date_condition` wraps `created_at` in `DATE()`, making it non-SARGable unlike the `start_date_condition`. - **`frontend/js/timeline.js`**: Adds `buildClusterChangelogMarkLines()` to map changelog timestamps onto chart x-axis indices, fetches changelog data when measurement-date sorting is active and a machine is selected, and injects a custom `'Cluster Changelog'` series with tooltip support. - **`frontend/js/helpers/main.js`**: `calculateStatistics` is refactored to use an internal `getNumericValue` helper instead of the `object_access` flag, handling plain numbers, `{value}` objects, and `[x, y]` array-format values. The `getNumericValue` helper silently returns `null` for `null` entries, which could cause wrong statistics without any error. - **`frontend/timeline.html`**: Default sorting changed from "Date of commit" to "Date of measurement" — this is a potentially breaking UI change for existing bookmarks. Gunicorn 25.2.0

New Features

  • Fast HTTP Parser (gunicorn_h1c 0.4.1): Integrate new exception types and limit parameters from gunicorn_h1c 0.4.1 for both WSGI and ASGI workers
    • Requires gunicorn_h1c >= 0.4.1 for http_parser='fast'
    • Falls back to Python parser in auto mode if version not met
    • Proper HTTP status codes for limit errors (414, 431)

Bug Fixes

  • uWSGI Async Workers: Fix InvalidUWSGIHeader: incomplete header error when using gevent or gthread workers with uwsgi protocol behind nginx. (#3552, [PR #3554](benoitc/gunicorn#3554))

  • FileWrapper Iterator Protocol: Add __iter__ and __next__ methods to FileWrapper for full PEP 3333 compliance. (#3396, [PR #3550](benoitc/gunicorn#3550))

Performance

  • ASGI HTTP Parser Optimizations: Improve ASGI worker HTTP parsing performance
    • Read chunks in 64-byte blocks instead of 1 byte at a time
    • Reuse BytesIO buffers with truncate/seek instead of creating new objects
    • Use bytearray.find() directly instead of converting to bytes first
    • Use index-based iteration for header parsing instead of list.pop(0)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary

This PR adds a Windows RAPL metric provider for measuring CPU energy consumption via the ScaphandreDrv kernel driver. The implementation uses a cmd.exe bridge to invoke the RAPL reader from WSL2.

## Changes

**Configuration**
- Updated `config.yml.example` with commented configuration for `CpuEnergyRaplScaphandreComponentProvider` including sampling rate and RAPL executable path

**Core Implementation**
- `provider.py`: New `CpuEnergyRaplScaphandreComponentProvider` class that:
  - Manages configurable sampling rate, rapl_reader_exe path, and disabled domains
  - Implements `check_system()` to verify driver availability
  - Extends metric invocation with executable path and domain parameters
  - Reports energy in microjoules (uJ)

**Windows C Binary**
- `rapl_reader_cli.c`: Windows native CLI tool that:
  - Reads RAPL MSR energy registers directly via ScaphandreDrv IOCTL
  - Supports domain filtering (CPU, DRAM, GPU, PSYS) with auto-detection
  - Uses monotonic performance counter timestamps with microsecond precision
  - Computes per-interval energy deltas with 32-bit wrap handling
  - Outputs timestamped energy data in GMT format

**Build & Bridge Scripts**
- `build_and_deploy.bat`: Windows batch script to compile and deploy `rapl_reader.exe` to `C:\rapl\`
- `metric-provider-binary`: Bash wrapper script that invokes the Windows RAPL reader via `cmd.exe` with options for sampling rate, domain exclusion, and driver checks

**Tests**
- Added `tests/usage_the_test.yml`: CPU and RAM stress test scenario using `stress-ng`

## Notes

Per PR discussion, the metric-provider-binary script was initially missing from the commit but has been added. The author acknowledged that calling bash directly via `subprocess.run` would be preferable and indicated intent to implement that improvement. The folder structure placement in the Windows-specific section (rather than common/component) was noted as a potential future refinement.

title: Added display resolutions to hardware_info
body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds display resolution detection to `hardware_info.py` by introducing `get_display_resoutions()`, which enumerates X11 sockets in `/tmp/.X11-unix/` and runs `xdpyinfo` for each display. The idea is sound, but the implementation has two bugs that will cause runtime failures and a minor naming typo. - **P0 – Eager invocation breaks `get_values`**: `get_display_resoutions()` is listed with `()` (call parentheses) on line 91, so the return value (a `str`) is stored in the list instead of the callable. When `get_values` later processes the list via `x[0](*x[2:])`, it calls `cf(result_string)` → `call_function("No Display")` → tries to invoke the string → `TypeError: 'str' object is not callable`. The fix is to remove the `()` so the function object is stored, consistent with how `read_rapl_energy_filtering` is used in `root_info_list`. - **P1 – `FileNotFoundError` on headless systems**: `os.listdir("/tmp/.X11-unix/")` raises `FileNotFoundError` when the directory does not exist (servers, CI, Docker without a display). A simple existence check or `try/except` before the `listdir` call is needed. - **P2 – Typo**: `resoutions` should be `resolutions` in both the function definition and its reference on line 91.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | lib/hardware_info.py | Adds `get_display_resoutions()` to collect X11 display resolutions via `xdpyinfo`, but the function is called with `()` at list-definition time (storing a string rather than the function reference), causing a `TypeError` at runtime when `get_values` attempts to invoke it through `cf`. Additionally, the function has no guard for the case where `/tmp/.X11-unix/` does not exist, which raises `FileNotFoundError` on headless systems. Minor typo in the function name (`resoutions` vs `resolutions`). | Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["Added display resolutions to hardware\_in..."](https://github.com/green-coding-solutions/green-metrics-tool/commit/3f6b1d0625288f20af4131a3ba07702dece0f0ec) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=26868410) > Greptile also left **3 inline comments** on this PR.
