(feat): CPU undersampling gated by not allowing more than 10ms sampling rate
body:
The issue was the average done on the values, not the sampling per-se.

When averaging over a 10ms timespan which we sampled at 1 ms we will always have 9 empty frames. Only one is meaningful. However this frame if carrying the info of being 100% utilization will then only be accounted for one frame. This means we average-away a lot of utilization by mapping it to a shorter timeframe than it actually happened in.

The best way to solve this is to clamp to 10 ms max

title: Runs in GMT issue warning in every run
body:
Currently runs issue 'Very few samples (< 50% of observed duration or < 2) encountered in phase '[BOOT]', MEAN values might be inaccurate' in every run.

This seems to be related to the new phase padding.

An unrelated sample seems to get mapped into the Boot phase which is typically zero (starting providers in boot phase - cgroup ones)

Needs further investigation.

For people experiencing this issues: To our current understanding it is more confusing than critical. NO values in other phases are affected.

title: Upgrading postgres memory parameters to 8 GB reasonable machine
body:
After running GMT in production for a while we see that some background jobs experience strong memory pressure and makes query partials spill to disk.

This PR addresses this by migrating from mini-developer-machine defaults to reasonable 8 GB dedicated defaults.

We assume every developer machine nowadays has at least 8 GB of memory and is not fully saturated when running GMT. Thus these configs should work everywhere out of the box and provide more long-term stability when deploying GMT in cluster mode without ever tuning configs by hand.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary

- Increased PostgreSQL memory settings in `docker/compose.yml.example` for 8 GB machines.
- Updated `shared_buffers`, `work_mem`, and `maintenance_work_mem` to reduce disk spills and improve background job stability.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: (rework): CarbonDB worker jobs now use 60 day window; Optimized backfill queries
body:
We are now using a 60 day window as we have seen errors when processing carbondb sometimes when backfill apis are not available for longer than 24 hours.

to not miss data while copying and compressing we now add an internal 30 buffer / grace period

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary

- Expands CarbonDB backfill/processing windows from ~24 hours to **60 days** and uses a **30-day grace/buffer** to prevent missing data when backfill/copy APIs lag.
- Refactors **carbon intensity** and **geo** backfills into a two-phase flow: run **DB-cache updates** for a computed set of missing rows, then manually fill only the **remaining** rows still missing values.
- Optimizes backfill queries by passing **explicit row ID lists** into cached update helpers (and simplifying the “missing” fetch helpers accordingly) rather than relying on broader null filters.
- Limits **compression** and related transformations to the **last 60 days** by changing the source query to a 60-day time window.
- Widens CarbonDB copy/merge/dedup operations to the **60-day** window (function defaults, constraint validation, and dedup cutoff logic updated).
- Updates `docker/structure.sql` with **new/adjusted indexes**, including partial indexes for missing geo backfills and a new `carbondb_data_raw(time, type, user_id)` index to improve performance (including compression-related access patterns).
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: (fix): Phase padding will only happen if phase had at least one sampl…
body:
…e present

We had the bug that the metric providers for cgroup, which come up later, get a metric mapped into their phase from the data coming after. This is misleading and should only be the case if the come up so early that they actually capture data from the phase.

With a long sleep it can be that the mapping for the next tick is multiple seconds away. Guarding that at least one sample occured in the phase helps as due to sampling rate watching by the provider itself we know that samples cannot be more than the expected sample rate apart from each other.

Closes https://github.com/green-coding-solutions/green-metrics-tool/issues/1774

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary

Updated phase metric aggregation to apply padding only when a phase contains in-phase samples. This prevents late-starting cgroup metrics from being incorrectly attributed to earlier phases and avoids false `[BOOT]` too-few-samples warnings.

## Changes

- Added in-phase sample tracking through SQL aggregation and derivative computation.
- Skipped result handling when phases have no in-phase samples.
- Updated low-sample warning text.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: (feat): Power Hog now also does not accept data anymore from older than 30 days
body:
Technically it could also accept older values, but to date there is no valid use case for it.

Having this in place helps us maintain the 30 day merge window for CarbonDB way easier as we can blindly copy over

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- Enforces a 30-day merge/timestamp acceptance window for Power Hog data on `POST /v2/hog/add`, rejecting timestamps older than the limit or in the future with HTTP 422 (and including the submitted timestamp in the error).

title: Fix repo URL generation to handle GitLab, Bitbucket, SSH, and local repos in the UI
body: Previously, commit and tree URLs were hardcoded to GitHub's `/commit/` and `/tree/` path format. This broke links for: - GitLab repos (which use `/-/commit/` and `/-/tree/`) - Bitbucket repos (use `/commits/` and `/src/`) - SSH-style URIs (e.g., `git@github.com:org/repo`) — not converted to HTTPS - Local paths — produced broken `file:///commit/...` links Changes: - Added `getRepoRefUrl(uri, type)` in `frontend/js/helpers/main.js` that normalizes URIs to HTTPS and selects the correct path convention per platform (GitHub /commit/, GitLab /-/commit/, Bitbucket /commits/) - Replaced inline `toHttpsUri(...)/commit/...` constructions in charts.js, stats.js, and timeline.js with the new helper - Removed the now-unnecessary `buildCommitLink()` function from stats.js - Non-HTTP URIs (local paths) now show commit info as plain text instead of a broken link - href attribute-breakout fixes — added `escapeString()` for user-controlled URL values interpolated into double-quoted href attributes (stats.js for `uri/relations.url/commit_link + commit_hash` and `main.js:createExternalIconLink`). - Updated `test_xss_protection_of_run_data` to prefix the payload with ">, so it actually breaks out of double-quoted attribute values (closing both the attribute and the surrounding start tag), exercising the href-escaping fixes that the previous plain payload silently skipped. Disclaimer: I used DeepSeek V4 Flash and GLM 5.2 for this PR. ## Summary - Added centralized repository URL generation for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, SSH, and local repositories. - Updated charts, stats, and timeline commit links to use the new helper. - Displayed local repository commits as plain text. - Escaped generated `href` attributes to prevent XSS vulnerabilities. - Added coverage for repository URL formats, local paths, and malicious attribute values. - Removed the obsolete `buildCommitLink()` helper.

title: Python version of phase_stats.py calculation
body:
This PR speeds up the processing for the phase stats by moving calculation out of the DB hotpath.

## Analysis
We first assumed the bottle neck was the SQL queries, which became quite complex, or the big database with the big index  (In our live DB of ~ 100 GB of raw measurement values)

However the slow down was the network connects. We make a separate SQL query per metric and phase. This can sum up to 6 x 30 calls easily. With setup and teardown each network call takes about 1 second.

Now we only do one big query to fetch all the values resulting in a 100x speedup

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary

- Replaced repeated per-phase, per-metric SQL aggregation with one time-ordered run query and in-memory Python calculations.
- Added PostgreSQL-compatible percentile interpolation, boundary samples, weighted averages, derivatives, and sampling-rate metrics.
- Updated carbon-intensity provider detection and handling by naming convention and unit.
- Added SCI metric derivation for phase-stat rebuild and replay tools.
- Renamed the carbon-intensity-level Electricity Maps provider and configuration key.
- Added `MAX_POSTGRES_BIGINT` for PostgreSQL-compatible integer handling.

title: (rework): Fronted moved away from async and moved to real threads
body: This PR reworks how the FastAPI routes work. We were using async routes so far. But due to the blocking nature of the SQL calls we could not really use the async feature of the uvicorn workers. This this PR moved all routes to non-async and python threads. They still have a GIL lock, but can through this also better share the postgresql connection pool, which is probably one of our most limiting factors. This PR is a draft and still needs some work: - Determining a good value for postgresql overall max connections - Increasing connection pool size - Determining good value for max workers and threads per worker - Benchmarking how much more performance we achieve through that approach ## AI background explanation on threads vs. async in our case threading.Thread in CPython is an OS thread. When you create one, CPython calls pthread_create (on Linux) under the hood. It's scheduled by the kernel just like any other thread — not a userspace/green-thread construct like a goroutine or a greenlet. The GIL doesn't change that; it just means only one of those OS threads is allowed to execute Python bytecode at any given instant. A thread blocked inside a C-level blocking syscall (like the recv() psycopg does while waiting on the Postgres socket) releases the GIL for that duration, which is exactly why handing blocking DB calls to a thread pool helps here. AnyIO's to_thread.run_sync doesn't spawn a fresh OS thread per call. It keeps a small pool of idle worker threads alive and reuses them (each one really is a threading.Thread/pthread that sits idle waiting for the next job), bounded by a CapacityLimiter — default 40 concurrent tokens per event loop. So per UvicornWorker process you get up to ~40 real, kernel-scheduled OS threads available to run blocking route bodies concurrently, on top of the one thread running the asyncio event loop itself. The new change is now: 8 Gunicorn processes → each with 1 event-loop OS thread + up to 40 AnyIO worker OS threads → each thread, while blocked on psycopg's socket I/O, releases the GIL so others can run → but only 2 of them per process can actually be talking to Postgres concurrently, since that's capped by lib/db.py:107's connection pool max_size=2. --- Need help on this PR? title: Rapl emi windows native
body: Add Windows EMI RAPL energy provider (cpu_energy_rapl_emi_component) Adds a new metric provider for Windows that reads CPU energy via the Windows Energy Meter Interface (EMI) — no custom kernel driver or test-mode required. The inbox Microsoft PPM driver on Windows 11 bridges RAPL MSRs to EMI automatically. What changed metric_providers/cpu/energy/rapl/emi/component/ — new provider: source.c (Win32 binary), provider.py (GMT wrapper), build.bat install_windows.ps1 — builds the EMI binary during installation config.yml.example — documents EMI provider in the Windows section frontend/js/helpers/config.js.example — display names for EMI metrics lib/phase_stats.py — maps cpu_utilization_windows_system/core to MEAN handler psu/energy/ac/xgboost/machine/provider.py — adds Windows CPU utilization as valid input source Validation Initial run on Windows 11 (Intel CPU) with both EMI and Scaphandre active simultaneously showed <1% deviation: EMI rapl_package0_pkg: 1.81 mWh / 14.47 W Scaphandre cpu_package: 1.96 mWh / 15.40 W Plan: extended local benchmark across multiple compression tools (gzip, zstd, bzip2, …) and file sizes to further validate driver consistency and cross-validate EMI vs. Scaphandre over a broader workload range. Results could also be compared against existing cluster measurements in the compression category? --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Overview This change adds Windows CPU energy and CPU utilization providers. The EMI provider reads RAPL energy through the Windows Energy Meter Interface. It uses the inbox Microsoft PPM driver. The change also adds two Windows CPU utilization providers and integrates them with metric mapping and PSU providers. ## Changes - **EMI RAPL energy provider** (`metric_providers/cpu/energy/rapl/emi/component/`): - `source.c` enumerates up to eight EMI devices. It emits per-channel energy deltas in GMT format. - `-i ` sets the sampling interval. The default is 99 ms. - `-c` checks availability and exits 0 when a usable device exists. - `provider.py` adds `CpuEnergyRaplEmiComponentProvider`. - `build.bat` compiles the binary with `cl.exe`. - **CPU utilization, system (Win32)** (`metric_providers/cpu/utilization/win32/system/`): - `source.c` uses `GetSystemTimes()`. The default interval is 1000 ms. - `provider.py` adds `CpuUtilizationWin32SystemProvider`. - `build.bat` compiles the binary. - **CPU utilization, per core (NTAPI)** (`metric_providers/cpu/utilization/ntapi/core/`): - `source.c` resolves `NtQuerySystemInformation` at runtime. It emits per-core busy percentages. - `--with-interrupt-dpc` adds per-core DPC and interrupt percentages. This option is off by default. - `provider.py` adds `CpuUtilizationNtapiCoreProvider`. - `build.bat` compiles the binary. - **Installer** (`install_windows.ps1`): - Builds the three new binaries after the Scaphandre build. - Uses `Start-Process -PassThru` and checks `.ExitCode`. - Searches for Visual Studio with `vswhere.exe` when `cl.exe` is not on the path. - Missing compiler or build failure produces a warning. - **Configuration and metrics**: - `config.yml.example` adds a commented EMI entry and an enabled system CPU utilization provider with sampling rate 99. It adds a commented per-core entry. - `frontend/js/helpers/config.js.example` adds display names and explanations for the two CPU utilization metrics. - `lib/phase_stats.py` classifies both CPU utilization metrics as MEAN. Only `cpu_utilization_win32_system` is added to machine-utilization selection. - **PSU providers**: - `psu/energy/ac/sdia/machine/provider.py` and `psu/energy/ac/xgboost/machine/provider.py` accept `cpu_utilization_win32_system` as a CPU utilization source. - The XGBoost provider also reads `cpu_utilization_win32_system.log`. ## Validation - The author reported a Windows 11 Intel comparison. EMI and Scaphandre ran at the same time. EMI measured 1.81 mWh (14.47 W). Scaphandre measured 1.96 mWh (15.40 W). - The author reported a 99 ms EMI and MSR comparison. The values were 84.607 mWh and 84.529 mWh. - The author reported sampling tests: - Direct binary tests showed negligible consecutive identical values at 1–99 ms. - GMT runs passed at 10 ms and above. They failed at 5 ms and 7 ms under the 20% sampling-rate tolerance. - The author attributed the failures to Windows `Sleep()` jitter. The author recommended a 10 ms minimum for GMT. - The author states that broader compression-workload validation is proposed. It is not reported as complete. - CI and build results: not available. ## Open items - A reviewer noted that the PSU XGBoost machine model is a submodule and should not be checked in. - The thread does not record which CodeRabbit questions were resolved. - A reviewer asked for `main` to be merged without force-pushing. The thread does not confirm the merge.

Changelog

Sourced from pytest-xdist's changelog.

pytest-xdist 3.8.0 (2025-06-30)

Features

  • [#1083](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1083) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1083>_: Add --no-loadscope-reorder and --loadscope-reorder option to control whether to automatically reorder tests in loadscope for tests where relative ordering matters. This only applies when using loadscope.

    For example, [test_file_1, test_file_2, ..., test_file_n] are given as input test files, if --no-loadscope-reorder is used, for either worker, the test_file_a will be executed before test_file_b only if a < b.

    The default behavior is to reorder the tests to maximize the number of tests that can be executed in parallel.

pytest-xdist 3.7.0 (2025-05-26)

Features

  • [#1142](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1142) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1142>_: Added support for Python 3.13.

  • [#1144](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1144) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1144>_: The internal steal command is now atomic - it unschedules either all requested tests or none.

    This is a prerequisite for group/scope support in the worksteal scheduler, so test groups won't be broken up incorrectly.

  • [#1170](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1170) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1170>_: Add the --px arg to create proxy gateways.

    Proxy gateways are passed to additional gateways using the via keyword. They can serve as a way to run multiple workers on remote machines.

  • [#1200](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1200) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1200>_: Now multiple xdist_group markers are considered when assigning tests to groups (order does not matter).

    Previously, only the last marker would assign a test to a group, but now if a test has multiple xdist_group marks applied (for example via parametrization or via fixtures), they are merged to make a new group.

Removals

  • [#1162](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1162) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1162>_: Dropped support for EOL Python 3.8.

  • [#1190](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1190) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/issues/1190>_: Switched to using a SPDX license identifier introduced in PEP 639.

  :func:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.pkcs7.pkcs7_decrypt_der`
  and its PEM and S/MIME variants no longer expose distinguishable errors or
  timing when unwrapping a ``RecipientInfo``'s ``encryptedKey``, which could
  act as a Bleichenbacher oracle for callers that decrypt untrusted messages.
  A random key is now substituted on failure, as described in :rfc:`3218`.
  Credit to **@X1AOxiang** for reporting the issue. **CVE-2026-69247**
* Deprecated Diffie-Hellman key exchange over finite fields (FFDH).
  Everything FFDH is deprecated, including the types in
  ``cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.dh`` and loading FFDH keys or
  parameters with the key loading APIs. Users should migrate to a more
  modern key exchange algorithm.
* Added ``xof()`` class methods to
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE128` and
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE256` for constructing
  algorithm instances configured for use with
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash`.
* The :mod:`X.509 verification <cryptography.x509.verification>` APIs are now
  considered stable and are subject to our API stability policy.
* Added the :doc:`/cobblestone` recipe, an implementation of the
  Cobblestone-128 and Cobblestone-256 instantiations of the `C2SP
  chunked-encryption specification
  <https://c2sp.org/chunked-encryption>`_ for streaming authenticated
  encryption of large messages.
* Parsing a Signed Certificate Timestamp list now rejects encodings that
  carry trailing bytes after the list or after an individual SCT, instead of
  silently ignoring them.
* Added support for using :class:`~cryptography.x509.Name` as a field type in
  the :doc:`/hazmat/asn1/index` module.
* Loading a public key or an EC private key now rejects DER where the
  ``subjectPublicKey`` (or EC ``publicKey``) ``BIT STRING`` declares a non-zero
  number of unused bits, instead of silently ignoring it.
* Parsing a CRL entry's ``InvalidityDate`` extension now rejects a
  ``GeneralizedTime`` that carries fractional seconds or another non-DER form,
  matching the strict encoding already required for every other X.509 time
  field.
* :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_request` and
  :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_response` now reject a request
  or response whose ``version`` field is not ``v1``, the only version defined
  by RFC 6960, matching the version validation already performed when loading
  certificates, CSRs and CRLs.
* :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash` is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
* HMAC (and therefore PBKDF2-HMAC) with SHA-3 hashes is now supported when
  building against AWS-LC.
* Diffie-Hellman (:doc:`/hazmat/primitives/asymmetric/dh`) is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.

title: Bump gunicorn from 26.0.0 to 26.1.0
body:
Bumps [gunicorn](https://github.com/benoitc/gunicorn) from 26.0.0 to 26.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from gunicorn's releases.

gunicorn 26.1.0

New Features

  • Glob patterns in reload_extra_files: entries containing *, ? or [ are treated as patterns, so ui/*/config.json watches every view's config without listing them one by one. Patterns are re-expanded on every reload check rather than once at startup, so a file created later starts being watched without restarting gunicorn, and ** recurses. A pattern matching nothing warns instead of failing, since with live expansion it may match later (#1643, #3662).

Security

  • Dependency floors raised past known advisories: every declared floor was checked against the advisory database. tornado, h2, setuptools and pymdown-extensions permitted vulnerable versions and now require the first clean release; pytest and httpx were unpinned and now carry floors. The tornado example pinned tornado<6, which was both the source of several advisories and older than the >=6.5.0 the tornado worker needs, so the example could not run as pinned.

Bug Fixes

  • SIGHUP did not reload the logger configuration: Arbiter.reload() re-read the configuration file but kept using the logger built at startup, calling only reopen_files() on its existing handlers. Changes to logconfig, logconfig_dict, logconfig_json and loglevel were ignored until a full restart, which in containers meant replacing the pod. The existing logger now re-runs its setup on reload, so new handlers, formats and levels take effect while the process identity and its listeners are preserved, and re-running the setup no longer stacks duplicate syslog handlers. An invalid log configuration on reload is not fatal either: the error is reported on stderr, the previous working configuration is restored and the master keeps running with it (#3353).

  • Truncated chunked bodies accepted: RFC 9112 section 7.1.2 ends a chunked body with 0 CRLF CRLF, the second CRLF being the mandatory empty trailer section. ChunkedReader.parse_chunk_size() swallowed the NoMoreData raised while scanning for it, so a body cut short right after the last chunk line was treated as complete instead of rejected. It now raises ChunkMissingTerminator (#3382, #3685).

  • --spew crashed on dynamically generated code: the trace hook indexed the 2-tuple returned by inspect.getsourcelines() by line number rather than indexing the list of lines, so a frame with no __file__ raised AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'rstrip' on line 1 and

Bumps [plotext](https://github.com/piccolomo/plotext) from 5.3.2 to 6.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from plotext's releases.

6.0.0

This s a complete rewrite of version 5.

To install it, as explained here, use:

pip install plotext --upgrade

Main changes

  • C++ kernel: the drawing is done by a new kernel written in C++, compiled during the installation.
  • The figure: plotext.figure is the plot, holding the tools necessary to build it, from the drawings to the way it looks and rendered; version 5 offered the same as separate functions of the package. When a grid of subplots is present, plotext.subplot() gives the subplot figure, holding the same tools.
  • Colored primitives: the pixel, holding a color pair and a style, the colorize string, and the matrix of colored characters a plot is made of.
  • The marker: a new object, plotext.marker, holding the symbol drawn at each point together with its coloring, in place of the marker parameter of version 5: it accepts a symbol name, a text of several characters, a colorize string or a whole matrix.
  • The signal: a sequence of points together with the settings describing how it is drawn. Every plotting method returns a signal object, which reaches the plot only when passed to plotext.figure.draw(). See the signal page.
  • The ruler: the object controlling the area of the plot where the numerical ticks appear. See the ruler page.
  • Command line tool: rewritten, the version 5 subcommands replaced by a chain of methods mirroring the Python ones.
  • Documentation: the readme files are replaced by a complete separate guide.
  • Pretty docstrings: the prettydoc module writes colorful docstrings, browsable one by one, as plotext.doc.bar(), or through the interactive menu plotext.doc(), inside the terminal.

The change log lists every renamed, removed and changed method, section by section.

title: Bump gunicorn from 26.1.0 to 26.2.0
body:
Bumps [gunicorn](https://github.com/benoitc/gunicorn) from 26.1.0 to 26.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from gunicorn's releases.

gunicorn 26.2.0

Cleartext HTTP/2 lands, and an HTTP/2 security fix.

Cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c)

http2_cleartext accepts prior-knowledge, upgrade, both or off (the default). Prior knowledge serves a connection that opens with the HTTP/2 preface; upgrade honours an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade: h2c request. Both work on the gthread, gevent and asgi workers.

This is for deployments where TLS is terminated by a proxy that speaks HTTP/2 upstream, so the hop into gunicorn no longer drops to HTTP/1.1. Only peers in forwarded_allow_ips are considered; everyone else is served HTTP/1.x exactly as if the setting were off. Each mechanism is enabled separately, so turning one on does not turn the other on.

Do not expose a cleartext HTTP/2 port to the internet.

Security

HTTP2Request built its headers straight from the stream, so nothing the HTTP/1 path enforces applied over HTTP/2: the underscore and header_map policy, duplicate Host and Content-Type, control characters in values, and the forwarded_allow_ips trust gate. An untrusted client could set SCRIPT_NAME and forge HTTP_* entries in the WSGI environ, and decide wsgi.url_scheme through :scheme. Both request classes now share one policy mixin, and the scheme comes from the transport.

If you serve HTTP/2, this is the reason to upgrade.

Other HTTP/2 fixes

WSGI responses were buffered whole before anything was sent; they stream now. HEAD, 204 and 304 no longer carry a body. Events read while blocked on a flow-control window were discarded, losing requests and body data outright. sendfile() is refused on HTTP/2 responses rather than bypassing framing.

Request bodies dropped on Upgrade requests

On the ASGI worker with the fast parser, any request carrying an Upgrade header reached the application with an empty body, whatever the header's value and with HTTP/2 switched off entirely. Fixed in gunicorn_h1c 0.6.9, which the fast extra now requires.

Full changelog: https://gunicorn.org/news/

Release notes

Sourced from pylint's releases.

v4.0.8

What's new in Pylint 4.0.8?

Release date: 2026-08-29

False Positives Fixed

  • Fix a false positive for :ref:unspecified-encoding when an open call uses a mode argument that cannot be inferred.

    Closes #10201

  • Fix a false positive for invalid-name (C0103) on names assigned in an if __name__ == "__main__": block. Such a block reads like a script body, so a name there is now accepted if it matches either the constant or the variable naming style.

    Closes #10766

  • Fix false positives for :ref:invalid-str-returned, :ref:invalid-repr-returned, :ref:invalid-format-returned, :ref:invalid-bytes-returned, :ref:invalid-hash-returned, :ref:invalid-index-returned, :ref:invalid-length-returned, :ref:invalid-length-hint-returned, :ref:invalid-getnewargs-returned and :ref:invalid-getnewargs-ex-returned when the returned value is an instance of a subclass of the expected builtin type, such as self in a str subclass or a namedtuple.

    Closes #11306

  • Fix false positives for :ref:bad-string-format-type when the argument is an instance of a subclass of int, float or str, such as bool or an IntEnum member formatted with %d.

    Closes #11315

False Negatives Fixed

title: Bump pytest-randomly from 4.1.0 to 5.0.0
body:
Bumps [pytest-randomly](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-randomly) from 4.1.0 to 5.0.0.
Changelog

Sourced from pytest-randomly's changelog.

5.0.0 (2026-09-01)

  • Support Python 3.15.

  • Shuffle tests in a wrapper around the pytest_collection_modifyitems hook, guaranteeing that the shuffle runs before all other plugins’ implementations of the hook.

    Previously, pytest-randomly shuffled in a plain tryfirst hook implementation. When another plugin also implemented the hook with tryfirst, as pytest-django does, whichever plugin pytest happened to register later ran first. Registration order comes from package metadata on disk, which can differ between seemingly identical environments — even two containers built from the same Dockerfile, or the same virtual environment after reinstalling a package. As a result, the same seed could yield different test orders in different environments. Worse, in environments where pytest-randomly ended up shuffling last, it silently destroyed the other plugin’s ordering — for pytest-django, the grouping of database tests that mirrors Django’s test runner (non-transactional database tests, then transactional ones, then the rest).

    Now the shuffle always runs first, and plugins that group tests with a stable sort apply their grouping on top of the shuffled order, so the final order is reproducible from the seed alone. In environments that previously hit the reversed hook order, upgrading changes the test order for a given seed — restoring both reproducibility and other plugins’ grouping.

    PR [#746](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-randomly/issues/746) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-randomly/pull/746>. Thanks to milssky for the report in Issue [#701](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-randomly/issues/701) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-randomly/issues/701>.

  • Require pytest 8+, the first version to require a version of pluggy that supports hook wrappers, as used by the above fix.

title: Bump plotext from 6.0.0 to 6.1.0
body:
Bumps [plotext](https://github.com/piccolomo/plotext) from 6.0.0 to 6.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from plotext's releases.

6.1.0

A maintenance release, mainly from three reports by henryiii.

  • Windows: two pieces of C++ that strict compilers refuse are gone, arrays taking their size while the program runs, and the words and, or and not in place of their symbols. They stopped conda-forge from building plotext (236).

  • macOS: the plot came out empty when the machine's alphabet setting was missing: plotext now turns it into utf-8 bytes itself, on every machine (237).

  • Large numbers: plots of large values stopped with an error about NaN. Every position is now held with twice the precision (238). The same loss of precision was naming the wrong day on a date axis, which is fixed with it.

  • Labels: large numbers on the ticks now reach the exponential form, and all the labels of a ruler share one form and one number of decimals.

  • Printing: show() now flushes python's output before drawing, and the plot's own after, so a print before the plot comes out before it, and a print after comes out after.

The whole list is in the change log, and the credits page now says where AI helped.

title: Bump uvicorn from 0.52.4 to 0.53.0
body:
Bumps [uvicorn](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn) from 0.52.4 to 0.53.0.
Release notes

Sourced from uvicorn's releases.

Version 0.53.0

🌐 Opt-in HTTP/2 support

uvicorn 0.53.0 adds experimental HTTP/2 through zttp, alongside a new zuvloop integration and connection-handling improvements.

uv add uvicorn==0.53.0
  • Serve HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 with zttp (#2982, #3101). Install zttp, then enable HTTP/2 with --http zttp --http2. Uvicorn negotiates HTTP/2 over TLS with ALPN and supports cleartext prior knowledge.
  • HTTP/2 remains experimental. Upgrade-based h2c and WebSockets over HTTP/2 are not supported.

⚙️ More event loop choice

  • Run Uvicorn with zuvloop (#3104). Install zuvloop separately and select it explicitly with --loop zuvloop on CPython 3.14 or newer.

🛡️ More reliable connections and proxies

  • Honor Connection: close token lists (#3103). Uvicorn now parses comma-separated tokens case-insensitively across HTTP implementations.
  • Trust IPv6 loopback proxies by default (#3119). The default FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS value now includes ::1.
  • Keep upgraded WebSockets alive (#3107). Uvicorn cancels the HTTP keep-alive timer when the connection becomes a WebSocket.

16.7 (2026-09-17)

Features ++++++++

  • Allow configuring only_rerun regular expressions in pytest.ini files. ([#165](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-rerunfailures/issues/165) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-rerunfailures/issues/165>_)

Match rerun_except against explicit __cause__ links only, so implicit except / finally context does not suppress reruns. title: Bump pylint from 4.0.8 to 4.0.9
body:
Bumps [pylint](https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint) from 4.0.8 to 4.0.9.
Release notes

Sourced from pylint's releases.

v4.0.9

What's new in Pylint 4.0.9?

Release date: 2026-09-23

Security Fixes

  • Someone without access to the configuration or linted code, but with access to the cache directory (predictable PYLINT_HOME on a multi-user host) can no longer write a crafted pickle that will runs arbitrary code when pylint access its stat cache. The result cache is now stored as JSON instead of pickle, preventing code-execution. The workaround is upgrading or not pointing PYLINT_HOME to an untrusted, shared, or group-writable directory. The default value, ~/.cache/pylint, is writable only by the user running pylint. (CVE with the same information pending)

False Positives Fixed

  • Fixed a false positive for no-self-use on a method that only uses self before a locally defined class (or other nested method), because the checker's could-be-a-function tracking state was not restored after visiting the nested method.

    Closes #3705

  • Fix a false positive for :ref:not-callable when calling functions constructed with types.FunctionType or types.LambdaType.

    Closes #7500

  • Fix a false positive for unnecessary-direct-lambda-call when a directly called lambda in a class body wraps a comprehension containing an assignment expression. PEP 572 makes that a SyntaxError without the lambda's scope, so following the message produced code that would not compile.

    Closes #9294

  • Fix a false positive for :ref:unnecessary-ellipsis when an ellipsis is the sole body statement of a method defined on a Protocol.

    Closes #9319

  • Fix a false positive for :ref:bad-exception-cause when the bases of the class being raised from cannot be inferred, such as an exception deriving from a C extension class. :ref:raising-non-exception and :ref:catching-non-exception already guard the same inherit_from_std_ex

Release notes

Sourced from uvicorn's releases.

Version 0.54.0

📨 Send metadata after the response body

uvicorn 0.54.0 adds response trailers and 103 Early Hints to its experimental HTTP/2 implementation through zttp.

uv add uvicorn==0.54.0 "zttp>=0.0.34"
  • Send HTTP/2 response trailers (#3146). The ASGI http.response.trailers extension lets applications send metadata, such as checksums, after the response body. Clients must send TE: trailers to receive them. Multiple trailer messages are combined before completing the response.
  • HTTP/2 remains experimental and opt-in. Enable it with --http zttp --http2. Upgrade-based h2c and WebSockets over HTTP/2 remain unsupported.

💡 Hint at resources before the final response

  • Send 103 Early Hints over HTTP/2 (#3137). Applications can use the ASGI http.response.early_hint extension to send resource hints before the final response. Each supplied link becomes a separate Link header.

title: Bump hiredis from 3.4.1 to 3.4.2
body:
Bumps [hiredis](https://github.com/redis/hiredis-py) from 3.4.1 to 3.4.2.
Release notes

Sourced from hiredis's releases.

3.4.2

This is a bugfix release. Users of hiredis-py 3.4.x that receive RESP3 push notifications — pub/sub deliveries or client-side cache invalidations — are encouraged to upgrade.

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Release the list each push notification is sized from (#239)

PushNotificationType_New pre-sized every PushNotification with a list that PyList_SetSlice only borrows, and the reference was never dropped. Each RESP3 push notification therefore stranded one list object for the lifetime of the process. Because push notifications carry pub/sub deliveries and client-side caching invalidations, the leak grew with message volume rather than with the number of connections, making it unbounded for a long-lived subscriber — roughly 20 MB per 200,000 four-element notifications, and more for larger ones. Dropping the reference also removes an allocation from the parse path, which makes parsing a small notification about 10% faster.

The same change checks PyList_New for failure and guards tryParentize against a NULL reply, so an allocation failure is now reported as an error instead of writing elements past the end of a zero-length notification.

RESP2 array replies were never affected.

Contributors

Thanks to @​mmick78 for finding and fixing this.

title: Update starlette requirement from >=1.6.0 to >=1.7.0
body:
Updates the requirements on [starlette](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from starlette's releases.

Version 1.7.0

This release adds experimental OpenTelemetry tracing, HTTP QUERY support, and response trailers in TestClient. Starlette now requires AnyIO 4.

[!WARNING] OpenTelemetryMiddleware is experimental. Its API and emitted telemetry may change in minor releases without a deprecation period.

Added

  • Add experimental OpenTelemetryMiddleware for HTTP server spans, with URL exclusions and custom tracer providers #3438, #3463, and #3520.
  • Expose the matched route through scope["route"] #3438.
  • Support the QUERY HTTP method in HTTPEndpoint, CORS, and OpenAPI 3.2 schema generation #3489.
  • Capture HTTP response trailers in TestClient and expose them through response.extensions["http.response.trailers"] #3563.
  • Support partitioned cookies in SessionMiddleware #3510.
  • Add partitioned to Response.delete_cookie() on Python 3.14 and later #3376.
  • Support IPv6 hosts in TrustedHostMiddleware and TestClient #3471.
  • Support Python 3.15 #3508.

Changed

  • Require anyio>=4.0.0,<5, dropping support for AnyIO 3 #3512.
  • Raise WebSocketDisconnected, a RuntimeError subclass, for disconnected WebSocket operations #2767.
  • Accept Collection[str] in CORSMiddleware configuration annotations, including sets and frozensets #3518.

Fixed

  • Run background tasks only after the response is sent when using BaseHTTPMiddleware #3476.
  • Return 400 for invalid multipart parser input #3492.
  • Include Vary: Origin on all normal CORS responses and vary preflight responses by all request headers that affect them #3516 and #3517.
  • Handle malformed Host headers and IPv6 authorities consistently across URL construction, host routing, and redirect middleware #3472.
  • Ignore Range headers when FileResponse has a status other than 200, preserving its status and full body #3568.
  • Handle standalone If-None-Match: * in StaticFiles #3201.

title: Fix git provider API branch lookup for branch names containing '#'
body: ## Problem Submitting a run through the API (or a watchlist entry) with a branch name containing `#` fails with a misleading error, e.g. for `task/#2259-gmt-setup`: > Could not find repository https://github.com/kadai-io/kadai and branch task/#2259-gmt-setup. Is the repo publicly accessible, not empty and does the branch task/#2259-gmt-setup exist? ## Root cause `lib/utils.py` interpolates the branch directly into the git provider API query string without URL-encoding: ```python url = f"{url}/commits?per_page=1&sha={branch}" ``` `#` starts a URL fragment, so everything after it is dropped before the request is sent. GitHub receives `sha=task/` instead of `sha=task/#2259-gmt-setup` and answers `404`, which surfaces as the incorrect "repo/branch not found" message. The branch itself is fine. ## Fix URL-encode the branch with `urllib.parse.quote(branch, safe='')` at all three interpolation sites: - `check_repo` — GitHub `sha=` - `get_repo_last_marker` — GitHub `sha=` and GitLab/custom `ref_name=` This also covers other URL-special characters a valid git ref may contain (space, `&`, `?`, etc.). ## Tests Added parametrized tests in `tests/lib/test_utils_git_api.py` asserting the branch round-trips intact through the captured request URL (query decoded back to the original, no fragment leaked) for branches containing `#`, space, `?`, and `&`, across `check_repo` (GitHub) and `get_repo_last_marker` (GitHub + GitLab). --- Need help on this PR? title: Comparing runs across the "Elephant" release fails with `Metric cannot be compared as units have changed: ugCO2e vs. ug`
body:
**What happens**

Comparing a pre-"Elephant" run with a current run fails:

```
Metric cannot be compared as units have changed: ugCO2e vs. ug
```

Example (private run comparison): https://metrics.green-coding.io/compare.html?ids=a0d07483-653a-4fd2-bff0-896ccda96f7e,59ce2670-046e-4911-b1bc-a9f618616002

**Why**

Before #1520 (`76ffc166`), energy-derived carbon metrics were written in `lib/phase_stats.py` with unit `'ug'`. After the rework they come from `lib/post_metric_providers/calculate_co2_intensity.py`, which writes `'ugCO2e'`.

The values are identical, only the label changed. But `api/api_helpers.py:658` (`get_phase_stats_object`) rejects the pair because the unit strings differ. Since phase stats are ordered by `created_at ASC`, the old run's `ug` is seen first and the new `ugCO2e` triggers the error.

No forward migration backfills the old `phase_stats` rows (checked all 57 migrations).

Note: `network_carbon_formula_global` and `embodied_carbon_share_machine` intentionally stayed `ug` in both versions, so only the `*_carbon_*` energy-derived metrics are affected.

**Options**

1. Forward migration to normalize history:
   ```sql
   UPDATE phase_stats
   SET unit = 'ugCO2e'
   WHERE unit = 'ug'
     AND metric LIKE '%_carbon_%'
     AND metric NOT IN ('network_carbon_formula_global', 'embodied_carbon_share_machine');
   ```
2. Treat `ug` and `ugCO2e` as equivalent in the compare unit check (matches `convert_value()`, which already handles both the same way).

**Question**

Which path do you prefer? Any pre-Elephant historical comparison is currently broken, so a backfill seems cleanest, but if old runs should keep their original unit label we'd need the equivalence approach instead.

title: fix: tolerate a truncated final powermetrics sample
body: Closes #286 Ending a measurement can fail while the powermetrics log is read. `read_metrics` splits the log on NUL and parses each fragment with `plistlib.loads`. Stopping powermetrics with SIGTERM, or leaving the last write buffered, can cut the final plist off before its root element closes. `plistlib.loads` then raises `ExpatError` ("no element found"), the handler prints the fragment and re-raises, and the runner reports a base exception from `stop_metric_providers`, dropping the samples that were already written. Following review, the provider now handles this the same way the base provider drops its last CSV line: if parsing fails on the last NUL-separated fragment, with `ExpatError` or `plistlib.InvalidFileException`, that fragment is dropped and the rows already parsed are kept. The `InvalidFileException` case covers an empty fragment after a trailing NUL. A parse failure on any earlier fragment still prints the fragment and raises. Tests in `tests/metric_providers/test_metric_provider_functions.py` build captures from the checked-in powermetrics log: a truncated last sample is dropped, a trailing NUL is ignored, and a truncated sample in the middle still raises. I did not run them locally, since the suite needs a full GMT install and its test containers. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

body:
Bumps [pylint](https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint) from 4.0.9 to 4.1.1.
Release notes

Sourced from pylint's releases.

v4.1.1

What's new in Pylint 4.1.1?

Release date: 2026-09-29

Other Changes

  • Pylint 4.1.0 could not be uploaded to PyPI, because it required an unreleased version of dill on Python 3.15, and PyPI refuses such a dependency. 4.1.1 is the first 4.1 release available on PyPI, see the 4.1.0 changes below.

    Refs #11495

v4.1.0

What's new in Pylint 4.1.0?

Release date: 2026-09-29

Startup is about 25% faster thanks to lazy imports. The import checker caches its isort configuration, which makes pylint about 17% faster on ansible. Finding the files to lint with --recursive=y no longer walks ignored directories such as .venv or node_modules, which took seconds on large trees. The duplicate-code checker and symilar also received optimizations that result in considerable performance improvements and memory use reduction on larger codebases. For example, pandas analysis went from 20 min to 55 s and pylint does not get OOM-killed when analyzing cpython anymore.

Python 3.15 support progresses: the unpacking in comprehensions added by PEP 798 no longer raises false positives, and the standard library deprecations of Python 3.15 are followed.

For CI, there is a new built-in junit output format (--output-format=junit), the NO_COLOR and FORCE_COLOR environment variables are respected, and the files to lint can now be set with the files option in the configuration file.

New checks: looping-through-iterator, impossible-comparison, chained-comparison-all-equal and using-comprehension-unpacking-in-unsupported-version.

Running with --jobs no longer duplicates the messages of extensions or ignores extensions enabled in the configuration.

Plugin authors: the confidence parameter can no longer be None, except in is_message_enabled, and the MSG_STATE_* constants are deprecated in favor of the MessageDisableReason enum.

The required astroid version is now 4.3.2. See the astroid changelog for additional fixes, features, and performance improvements applicable to pylint.

title: fix(playwright): fail fast on IPC errors via single status FIFO
body:
> **AI disclaimer:** Parts of this pull request were generated with AI assistance. Please review carefully.

## Problem

A cached website run (`templates/website/usage_scenario_cached.yml`) failed with:

```
RuntimeError: Error: Page was not accessible. HTTP Return code 503.
Executed command that produced error: if (!page_result.ok()) throw `Page was not accessible. HTTP Return code ${page_result.status()}`
```

Two issues made this failure slow and opaque:

1. When a Playwright command threw, the IPC callback re-threw inside an async `data` handler whose promise was ignored. That produced an `UnhandledPromiseRejection` and crashed the node process. The error file was written, but the ready FIFO was never signaled, so the runner only noticed after its process timeout (~600 s).
2. Status signalling was spread over two FIFOs plus a plain error file, with a two-step `cat ready; cat error` in the runner.

## Changes

- `templates/partials/gmt-playwright-ipc.js`
  - Replaced `/tmp/playwright-ipc-ready` and `/tmp/playwright-ipc-error` with a single `/tmp/playwright-ipc-status` FIFO.
  - The command handler writes `ok` on success or `error: <message>` on failure, and no longer re-throws (which previously crashed the process).
- `lib/scenario_runner.py`
  - Reads `/tmp/playwright-ipc-status` in one blocking `cat` and raises immediately on anything other than `ok`. An empty read means the IPC process died without reporting a status.
  - The timeout branch reports that no status was received within the allotted time. The old error-file read is gone because a hard crash never wrote it anyway.
- 4 `templates/partials/gmt-playwright*.yml` templates: the browser-launch rendezvous now checks for `/tmp/playwright-ipc-status`.

Note: an earlier revision of this PR also added a non-2xx check to the warmup helper. That was dropped: status policy belongs to the scenario's `Check HTTP Status Code` step, and the shipped website scenario already enforces 2xx there.

## Testing

- `node --check` and `python3 -m py_compile` pass.
- Local FIFO simulation: success and failure statuses are both delivered immediately instead of after the process timeout.

## Notes / risk

- No Docker + browser integration test (requires the Playwright container), so the end-to-end path is not exercised in CI.
- Rename of the FIFO: anything outside this repo hardcoding `/tmp/playwright-ipc-ready` would break.

title: Bump pytest-playwright from 0.9.0 to 0.10.0
body:
Bumps [pytest-playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-pytest) from 0.9.0 to 0.10.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pytest-playwright's releases.

v0.10.0

Highlights

Traces for playwright.request API contexts (#333). --tracing now also records contexts created with playwright.request.new_context(), one chunk per test, so a session-scoped API context yields a trace per test. The traces follow the same retain-on-failure handling, trace-N.zip naming and report attachments as browser traces. Requires Playwright 1.60 or newer.

Artifacts in test reports (#332). Kept screenshots, videos and traces are added to the teardown report as playwright_screenshot, playwright_video and playwright_trace user properties, so --junitxml writes them as <property> elements and pytest_runtest_logreport hooks and reporters can pick them up. With pytest-html >= 4 they are linked from the report, and embedded with --self-contained-html.

Reruns keep their own artifacts (#331). With pytest-rerunfailures, every attempt now writes to its own folder, test-results/<test>-retry1/ and so on, like Playwright Test. Attempts no longer overwrite each other.

Artifacts survive fixture failures in teardown (#330). --tracing retain-on-failure, --video retain-on-failure and --screenshot only-on-failure now keep artifacts when a fixture fails during teardown. A test skipped from a fixture no longer counts as failed.

Per-test browser launch options (#329):

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "browser_type_launch_args",
    [{"args": ["--lang=de-DE"]}],
    indirect=True,
)
def test_german(page):
    ...

Each distinct value launches its own browser; command line options such as --headed and --slowmo still apply.

Multi-browser parametrization fixes. Overriding the page fixture no longer drops --browser parametrization on older pytest versions (#314). browser_name is now parametrized indirectly, so tests keep their original order within a browser (#284).

VS Code debugger (#328). The browser is launched headed under the debugger only when a display is available. On Linux without DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY set, it stays headless unless --headed is passed.

Breaking changes

  • pytest-base-url is now an optional dependency (#334). The plugin provides --base-url, the base_url ini option, the PYTEST_BASE_URL environment variable and the base_url fixture on its own. --verify-base-url needs the extra:

    pip install pytest-playwright[base-url]

  • Minimum pytest version is 7.0 for pytest-playwright and 8.2 for pytest-playwright-asyncio (#333).

title: Bump pylint from 4.1.2 to 4.1.3
body:
Bumps [pylint](https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint) from 4.1.2 to 4.1.3.
Release notes

Sourced from pylint's releases.

v4.1.3

What's new in Pylint 4.1.3?

Release date: 2026-10-11

False Positives Fixed

  • Fixed a false positive for attribute-defined-outside-init when an attribute is assigned inside the setter of an old-style, non-decorator property(fget, fset) call. The decorator form (@property / @x.setter) was already exempted by the fix for #409; the classic call form was not.

    Closes #3325

  • Fix a false positive for used-before-assignment when a name bound by an earlier target of the same assignment is used by a later target, as in a = b[a] = 0.

    Closes #5955

  • Fix a no-member false positive in a comprehension inside a branch that cannot run, such as if sys.platform == "win32": on Linux. Like the rest of the branch, the comprehension is no longer checked for missing members.

    Closes #7240

  • Fix a false positive for used-before-assignment when a name bound by a tuple or list target of a with item is used by a later item of the same with statement.

    Closes #7545

  • Fix false positives such as not-callable, not-an-iterable, unpacking-non-sequence and no-member on the result of a function whose body is only ..., like @overload and .pyi stubs. Such calls were inferred as returning None. This affected sqlalchemy.func, pydantic.Field, and the torch functions wrapped by _add_docstr, such as torch.linalg.qr.

    Closes #8138 Closes #9218 Closes #9354 Closes #10087

  • Fix a false positive for protected-access when a subclass of a subscripted generic base, such as class Child(Parent[T]), accesses a protected member through that base, such as Parent._foo(self).

    Closes #8600

Release notes

Sourced from starlette's releases.

Version 1.8.0

This release adds HTTP 103 Early Hints, preserves response trailers through GZipMiddleware, and stops FileResponse transfers when clients disconnect. Starlette now requires Python 3.11.

Added

  • Add Request.send_early_hints() for HTTP 103 Early Hints through the ASGI http.response.early_hint extension #3435.

Changed

  • Require Python 3.11 or later, dropping support for Python 3.10 #3592.
  • Exclude native gRPC media types (application/grpc and application/grpc+...) from GZipMiddleware compression by default #3565.
  • Send http.response.start immediately in GZipMiddleware for responses with an existing Content-Encoding, status 206, or an excluded content type, instead of waiting for the first body chunk #3631.
  • Resolve the multipart charset once per request instead of once per field #3618.

  • Stop FileResponse transfers when the client disconnects #3523.
  • Stop multipart range responses when the file ends before a range is complete, instead of looping forever #3583.

  • Include Allow: GET, HEAD in StaticFiles 405 responses #3640.
  • Close Request.stream() generators deterministically, avoiding "Exception ignored" errors with stacked BaseHTTPMiddleware #3628.

title: Removing -it arguments for docker run
body: The -it arguments had no functional reason for what we are doing with the container as we send no input and do not want to appear as a terminal. The initial reason was that by attaching a terminal some containers stay open, which is what GMT needs. However we introduced 'entrypoint' overriding as a feature a while ago so the user can set entrypoing: tail -f /dev/null if really needed. This is much cleaner than having this hack. Furthermore by removing -t we gain cleaner logs as tools do not think that a terminal is attached and thus do not bring in ANSI codes into the output. --- Need help on this PR? body:
Bumps [fastapi](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi) from 0.143.3 to 0.150.0.
Release notes

Sourced from fastapi's releases.

0.150.0

When no file is selected, browsers submit a file part with an empty filename and empty content. FastAPI now treats this as missing: required file fields return a validation error, and fields with defaults or default factories use them. Unselected inputs are ignored in lists of files. Named zero-byte files are still accepted.

Breaking Changes

  • 🐛 Treat unselected browser file inputs as missing. PR #16534 by @​tiangolo.

0.149.0

Browsers submit empty text inputs as empty strings (""). FastAPI now treats empty scalar form values as missing in form models, matching individual Form parameters. Required fields return a validation error. Fields with defaults or default factories use them and remain unset in model_dump(exclude_unset=True).

Empty strings inside lists are preserved. Omitted boolean form fields still become False. JSON requests and direct Pydantic validation are unchanged.

Breaking Changes

  • 🐛 Treat empty scalar values as missing in form models. PR #16529 by @​tiangolo.

0.148.0

Defaults for omitted Query, Header, Cookie, and Form parameters and model fields are no longer treated as user input. Defaults are not validated unless validate_default=True is enabled. If you rely on validators running for omitted values, enable default validation with Field(validate_default=True) for model fields or, for example, Query(validate_default=True) for individual parameters. Body(validate_default=True) is now honored too.

For parameter models, applying a default no longer marks a field as explicitly set, so model_dump(exclude_unset=True) excludes it. Default factories run once, and validation errors no longer include injected defaults in input.

Omitted boolean form fields still become False and count as explicitly set.

0.147.0

Omitted bool and bool | None form fields are now interpreted as False, matching unchecked HTML checkboxes. title: fix(frontend): order time series notes comparison like the comparison tables
body:
## Problem

On `compare.html`, the time series notes history chart and its "notes differ" message use the opposite run order from the rest of the page, so the message reads `Run 2 -> Run 1` instead of `Run 1 -> Run 2`.

## Root cause

Two orderings are in use:

1. The `ids` URL parameter is built from the checked rows in the runs table (`frontend/js/helpers/runs.js`), which is fed by `/v1/runs` ordered by `created_at DESC`. So `run_ids[0]` is the **newest** run.
2. `/v1/compare` orders `comparison_details` and the phase stats by `created_at ASC` (`api/api_helpers.py`), i.e. the first table column, and the first "Run 1" label, is the **oldest** run. `/v1/diff` sorts the same way.

`fetchAndShowTimeSeriesNotesHistory()` consumed the URL order, so its "Run 1"/"Run 2" series, the ⚠ diff markers and the `a -> b` entries in the "same amount of notes, but at least one note differed" message were all listed newest-first, while the tables directly above them list oldest-first.

Example (repo fixture `tests/data/json/compare-f4ed967e-7c27-4055-815f-ea437fc11d25,a416057b-235f-41d8-9fb8-9bcc70a308e7.json`): URL ids `f4ed967e (2024-09-13), a416057b (2024-09-11)`, but `comparison_details` lists `a416057b` first. The note diff was printed 09-13 -> 09-11 while the tables number 09-11 as run 1.

## Change

One line in `frontend/js/compare.js`: feed `comparison_details` order to `fetchAndShowTimeSeriesNotesHistory()` instead of the raw URL `ids`. Same grouping and ordering as `comparison_identifiers`, so the notes chart matches the table columns.

## Not changed

`/v1/diff` already sorts server-side. The step delta is now `newer - older`, so its colors match the legend; values change sign vs. before, magnitudes not.

## Testing

- `node --check frontend/js/compare.js`
- Manual: compare two runs where the notes text changed; the problem list and the ⚠ markers now read in the same run order as the phase stat tables.

title: Update starlette requirement from >=1.8.0 to >=1.10.0
body:
Updates the requirements on [starlette](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from starlette's releases.

Version 1.10.0

📝 Leaner URL-encoded form parsing

Starlette 1.10.0 parses URL-encoded forms with less memory and CPU, no longer drops the last field when a stream ends early, and lets you compare FormData that holds several uploads under one key.

uv pip install starlette==1.10.0
  • Forms with many fields parse faster and use less memory (#3724). FormParser builds each field in the parser callbacks instead of queueing every event and replaying it. On CodSpeed, 1000 fields went from 42.8 ms to 34.9 ms and from 63.5 KB to 54.5 KB, and the max_fields limit case went from 6,880 B to 864 B.
  • The last field is kept when the request stream ends without an empty chunk (#3599). The parser is now finalized once the stream is exhausted, so custom streams that never yield a final b"" no longer lose their last field.
  • FormData with repeated uploads can be compared (#3619). Comparing two FormData objects with several UploadFile values under the same key used to raise TypeError.

⚠️ Behaviour changes

  • Multidict equality keeps the order of values under a repeated key (#3619). Keys can still appear in any order, but QueryParams("a=1&a=2") and QueryParams("a=2&a=1") are no longer equal, matching what getlist() returns.
  • starlette.formparsers.FormMessage is deprecated (#3724). The parser no longer uses it, and FormParser.messages is gone. Calling FormMessage(...) emits a StarletteDeprecationWarning.

🧭 Routing and URL generation

  • Path parameter values that look like a placeholder are kept as they are (#3725). url_path_for("route", category="{id}", id="42") on /{category}/{id} now returns /{id}/42 instead of /42/42. Substitution also got faster, from 549 ns to 520 ns with two parameters and from 1,078 ns to 779 ns with five.
  • Route matching does less work per request (#3665, #3722). Match members are compared by identity, cutting up to 4.9% of the instructions per dispatch in the routing benchmarks.
  • WSGIMiddleware strips root_path only at a path segment boundary (#3718). A request to /application under a root_path of /app no longer becomes /lication.
  • FloatConvertor reports NaN and infinity correctly (#3716). NaN was reported as a negative float.

🛡️ Middleware, responses and config

  • Handled exceptions no longer keep requests alive (#3205). Starlette clears the traceback after an exception handler runs, so an exception instance reused across requests, such as a module-level HTTPException, no longer pins per-request objects in memory.
  • Middlewares accept http.response.start without headers (#3721). BaseHTTPMiddleware, GZipMiddleware and SessionMiddleware default the omitted field to an empty list instead of raising KeyError.
  • FileResponse ignores Range on methods other than GET and HEAD (#3679). A POST endpoint that returns a file now sends the full file, as RFC 9110 requires.
  • Config strips one pair of matching outer quotes from env file values (#3720). KEY='say "hi"' now reads as say "hi" instead of say "hi.

Full changelog: 1.9.0...1.10.0

Changelog

Sourced from starlette's changelog.

1.10.0 (October 24, 2026)

Changed

  • Compare multidicts such as FormData and QueryParams by key while keeping the order of values under a repeated key, so FormData with repeated uploads no longer raises TypeError. QueryParams("a=1&a=2") and QueryParams("a=2&a=1") are no longer equal #3619.
  • Build URL-encoded form fields in the parser callbacks, lowering memory and CPU usage for forms with many fields #3724.
  • Compare Match members by identity during routing #3665 and #3722.

Deprecated

  • Deprecate starlette.formparsers.FormMessage, which is no longer used #3724.

Fixed

  • Parse the last URL-encoded form field when the request stream ends without an empty chunk #3599.
  • Keep path parameter values that look like another placeholder in url_path_for() #3725.
  • Default omitted http.response.start headers in BaseHTTPMiddleware, GZipMiddleware and SessionMiddleware instead of raising KeyError #3721.
  • Clear the traceback of handled exceptions, so reused exception instances no longer keep per-request objects alive #3205.
  • Strip only one pair of matching outer quotes from Config env file values #3720.
  • Strip root_path from PATH_INFO only at a path segment boundary in WSGIMiddleware #3718.
  • Report NaN and infinity correctly in FloatConvertor.to_string() #3716.
  • Ignore Range on requests other than GET and HEAD in FileResponse #3679.

1.9.0 (October 18, 2026)

Changed

  • Stream TestClient response bodies, so client.stream() returns before the application finishes. Closing an unfinished streamed response now cancels the application #3491.

Fixed

  • Percent-encode ?, #, \ and a leading // in the request path when building request.url, and \ and a leading // in url_path_for #3671.
  • Use the byte length for Content-Length when the response body is a typed or multidimensional memoryview #3622.
  • Include HEAD in the Allow header of HTTPEndpoint 405 responses when GET is defined #3585.
  • Match host names case-insensitively in Host routing and TrustedHostMiddleware #3542.
  • Preserve every existing Vary header in MutableHeaders.add_vary_header(), used by GZipMiddleware and SessionMiddleware #3675.

1.8.0 (October 13, 2026)

This release drops Python 3.10 support and adds HTTP 103 Early Hints.

Added

  • Add Request.send_early_hints() for HTTP 103 Early Hints through the ASGI http.response.early_hint extension #3435.

Changed

  • Require Python 3.11 or later, dropping support for Python 3.10 #3592.
  • Exclude native gRPC media types (application/grpc and application/grpc+...) from GZipMiddleware compression by default #3565.
  • Send http.response.start immediately in GZipMiddleware for responses with an existing Content-Encoding, status 206, or an excluded content type, instead of waiting for the first body chunk #3631.

... (truncated)

title: Select the displayed phase and flow via URL query parameters
body:
## What I want

The detailed metrics page should accept normal query parameters next to the existing run id, so a link can point at an exact view:

- `stats.html?id=<run>&phase=BOOT` opens the BOOT phase.
- `stats.html?id=<run>&phase=RUNTIME&flow=<flow name>` opens Runtime with that flow selected instead of the aggregated "All Flows" view.
- Without parameters nothing changes: Runtime / All Flows stays the default.

Clicking a phase or flow tab should also write the matching query parameters into the browser address bar, so the currently displayed view can always be copied as a URL. This matches how the rest of the frontend passes state through the query string.

The same applies to `compare.html`, which uses the same phase/flow tabs and the same selection helper, so the feature should work there as well.

## Proposed solution

Extend the phase-selection helper in `frontend/js/helpers/phase-stats.js` to read `phase` and `flow` from the query string and drive the same tab selection it already performs for a run's phases and flows. Because the helper is shared, `stats.html` and `compare.html` are both covered. It runs after all tabs are built, so the targets exist; validation is reused and unknown or malformed values fall back to Runtime / All Flows.

Add the reverse direction: when a phase or flow tab is selected, update the browser URL with the corresponding parameters (keeping the run id), without adding history entries. Hook this into the existing tab click handlers.

No API or backend change is needed: the phase stats endpoint already returns every phase and flow of a run.

Document the parameters on the page where flow selection is explained, and note that the `&phase=` used on badge image URLs is a different parameter with a different format. Add Playwright tests in `tests/frontend/test_frontend.py` using the existing fixture that contains a flow phase, asserting the correct tabs are active when the parameters are present and that clicking a tab updates the URL.

## Open questions

- Does the feature make sense at all, and is the URL-update-on-click behaviour wanted, or should the address bar stay untouched?
- Which form should `phase` accept: `RUNTIME`, `[RUNTIME]`, or both?
- Should `flow` without `phase` imply Runtime, or be ignored?
- Invalid values: silent fallback to Runtime / All Flows, or a notification?

@ArneTR Let me know what you think about this idea 😊

title: Bump pytest from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0
body:
Bumps [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

Release notes

Sourced from owenthereal/action-upterm's releases.

v2.8.0

Highlights

  • Guest tools. Three new inputs let guests do more than share the session's terminal. All three are off by default. They need upterm v0.41.0 or newer, which the action installs by default. Before the session starts, the action checks each input you turn on against upterm host --help.
    • allow-exec: true runs guests' commands without approval: ssh SESSION CMD, and VS Code Remote-SSH.
    • allow-forwarding: loopback lets guests forward ports to the runner's literal loopback addresses, 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1.
    • full-access: true does both, and also lets guests transfer files: what an SSH login to the runner's account can do. It requires limit-access-to-actor or limit-access-to-users.
  • Ready-to-paste SSH config. With upterm v0.41.0, the step prints upterm's ~/.ssh/config block and the relay's known_hosts line in its log and in the job summary. A new ssh-config output carries the same text, plus a commented LocalForward 127.0.0.1:… line for reaching a service on the runner.
  • VS Code. The README walks through debugging a failing job with VS Code Remote-SSH:
    1. Pin the relay key, once per device.
    2. Add Include ~/.ssh/upterm-gha.conf to your ssh config, once.
    3. Paste each job's block into that file.
    4. Connect.
    5. Reach ports on the runner with LocalForward 127.0.0.1:L 127.0.0.1:R.

Notes

  • Commands need a grant. upterm v0.41.0 runs an explicit SSH command (ssh … CMD) privately. In the action's sessions it runs only with allow-exec or full-access, because nothing on the runner can approve it. Plain ssh still joins the shared terminal. See upterm v0.41.0.
  • Nothing existing changes. All existing inputs and outputs work as before.

title: Prio ordering
body:
This PR introduces A priority system for the jobs queue.

Users with a higher priority get processed first. Internally they get shuffeld still though if the processing mode of the machine is *random*.



<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary

- Waiting jobs are ordered by user priority, with higher priorities processed first. Missing priorities default to `0`.
- Jobs with equal priority use the configured selection order: random or oldest-created first.
- Tests cover priority ordering in both processing modes, FIFO ordering for equal priorities, and the default priority.
- The default seed data includes three additional schedule modes: `commit-variance`, `tag-variance`, and `statistical-significance`.

  • Fix ~Connection.cancel_safe() failing if the cancel connection is not ready immediately, for instance on a slow network (:ticket:[#1440](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1440)).
  • Fix reference cycles created adapting recursive types, which kept data in memory until the next garbage collection (:tickets:[#1443](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1443), [#1462](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1462)).

title: Carbon Backfilling Rework
body: - Removed DB caching and moved to only memory caching; - Using History Endpoint of Elephant and allowing 6+ hours backfilling grace window --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Reworks carbon-intensity backfilling to use Elephant’s history endpoint instead of the database cache. It selects missing values from the configured CarbonDB merge window and uses measurement time to choose the closest final data point from the preferred provider. Rows wait for the configured period before the job uses another available provider or a bundled yearly average. Request fences and buckets control the history queries. Removes the `carbon_intensity` table and adds a migration to drop it. CarbonDB copy-over skips rows without carbon data, and validation allows the configured wait period plus one hour. Adds country lookup for eligible IPs with client-supplied coordinates. Updates example configurations and adds backfill tests.

title: (fix): Resolve green-coding-redis-container on the codespace host
body: In a GitHub Codespace, a measurement run with optimizations enabled writes this to `system_logs`: ``` Error: Redis store_artifact failed Exception (ConnectionError): Error -2 connecting to green-coding-redis-container:6379. Name or service not known. ``` ## Cause `optimization_providers/base.py` calls `get_phase_stats_single` from `api/scenario_runner` in the runner process instead of over HTTP, and that function ends with `store_artifact(ArtifactType.STATS, ...)`, which connects to the redis host from `config.yml`: `green-coding-redis-container:6379`. On the host that name only resolves through `/etc/hosts`. `lib/install_shared.sh` writes `127.0.0.1 green-coding-postgres-container green-coding-redis-container`, `.devcontainer/on-start.sh` wrote the postgres name only. So in a codespace postgres resolves and redis does not: the error only shows up in codespaces, only on the optimizations path, and it survives container restarts. ## What is not the cause Container networking and startup order, measured in the codespace while the errors were being logged: - `getent hosts` inside `green-coding-gunicorn-container` resolves both `green-coding-postgres-container` (172.18.0.2) and `green-coding-redis-container` (172.18.0.4). - all three containers are on `green-metrics-tool_default`. - redis: `RestartCount=0`, exit code 0, not OOM-killed; it started 90 ms before gunicorn and the last error was logged 81 s after that start. - the `127.0.0.1:6379` publish in `docker/compose.yml` is host-only and is not used by this path. `--skip-optimizations` hides the error because `optimization_providers/base.py` is then never called. ## Change `on-start.sh` writes the same hosts entry as `install_shared.sh`. ## Verification Verified in a codespace with the hosts entry in place. The rows from before the fix stay in the table, so the check is that a run with optimizations enabled adds none: ```sh date docker exec green-coding-postgres-container psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 9573 -U postgres -d green-coding \ -c "select created_at from system_logs where message ilike '%store_artifact%' order by created_at desc limit 5;" ``` ``` Mon Nov 9 12:16:42 UTC 2026 created_at ------------------------------- 2026-11-09 12:55:44.446523+01 2026-11-09 12:39:30.759096+01 2026-11-09 12:35:51.869978+01 2026-11-09 11:27:38.904498+01 (4 rows) ``` The run finished at `12:16:42 UTC`, the newest error row is `12:55:44+01` (= `11:55:44 UTC`), 21 minutes before it. Non-codespace installs were already fine: a local install has the combined line in `/etc/hosts` and both names resolve to `127.0.0.1`. ## Impact of the bug Lost cache write plus one error row per run. `store_artifact` catches the exception, so the phase stats are still computed and returned and the optimizations still run. --- _Created by pi (AI agent), reviewed by me._ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
