title: Bump psycopg from 3.3.8 to 3.3.9
body:
Bumps [psycopg](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg) from 3.3.8 to 3.3.9.
Changelog

Sourced from psycopg's changelog.

.. currentmodule:: psycopg

.. index:: single: Release notes single: News

psycopg release notes

Current release

Psycopg 3.3.9 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^

  • Use the C implementation of the wait functions on Windows too. It was disabled because of an excessive CPU usage, fixed in Psycopg 3.2.11 (:ticket:[#645](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/645)).
  • Fix binary dumping of !Int4Range and other typed ranges and multiranges (:ticket:[#1157](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1157)).
  • Fix dumping of Decimal 0 with large exponent (part of :ticket:[#1414](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1414)).
  • Close the connection if the query cancellation following a Ctrl-C or a task cancellation is interrupted again, instead of leaving it stuck in ACTIVE state (:ticket:[#1435](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1435)).
  • Limit the memory used by :sql:COPY FROM if the server consumes data slower than it is produced. Add a !flush_threshold parameter to ~copy.LibpqWriter to tune it (:ticket:[#1437](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1437)).
  • Don't wait on the event loop when the socket is already writable, which made pipeline mode, ~AsyncCursor.executemany() and ~AsyncCopy.write() on async connections several times slower than on sync ones (:ticket:[#1468](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1468)).
  • Fix client-side quoting of negative zero floats and decimals, which could produce a -- SQL comment (:ticket:[#1480](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1480)).
  • Raise DataError instead of !ValueError registering a composite whose name or attributes are not valid namedtuple names, for instance Python keywords (:ticket:[#1482](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1482)).
  • Speed up the C implementation of the sync wait function, in particular when the connection doesn't need to wait, for instance at every ~Copy.write() (:ticket:[#1484](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1484)).
  • Don't replace the exception raised in a :sql:COPY block, for instance an interruption, with an error terminating the operation (:ticket:[#1486](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1486)).
  • Fix ~copy.QueuedLibpqWriter hanging forever, instead of raising the error, if sending data to the server fails while its queue is full (:ticket:[#1489](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1489)).
  • Performance improvements to lists dumping (:tickets:[#1490](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1490), [#1491](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1491)).
  • 2.5x faster UUID loading in the C implementation (:ticket:[#1494](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/issues/1494)).
  • Reduce the size of the binary packages by about 15 to 40%, depending on the platform.

title: Bump gunicorn from 26.2.0 to 27.0.1
body:
Bumps [gunicorn](https://github.com/benoitc/gunicorn) from 26.2.0 to 27.0.1.
Release notes

Sourced from gunicorn's releases.

gunicorn 27.0.1

Bug Fixes

  • ASGI: serve the next request on a kept-alive HTTP/1.1 connection as soon as the previous response is complete. It used to wait until the application returned, so a background task (Starlette, FastAPI) held up every request behind it on the same connection (#3819).
  • ASGI: refuse an informational (1xx) response sent after the final response has started, instead of writing it out of order (RFC 9110 §15.2).
  • gthread: when a worker stops (max_requests, reload, SIGTERM), keep its kept-alive connections open for up to 2 seconds and answer a request that arrives on one with Connection: close, instead of closing them right away. A client reusing such a connection, such as one following a redirect, lost its request (RFC 9112 §9.6) (#3821).

Full changelog: https://github.com/benoitc/gunicorn/blob/master/docs/content/news.md

gunicorn 27.0.0

Breaking Changes

  • Reject with 400 a request whose Transfer-Encoding does not end with chunked, such as gzip or identity alone, with or without Content-Length (RFC 9112 §6.3). The WSGI workers used to read such a body until the connection closed and the ASGI worker treated it as empty. Clients that send Transfer-Encoding: identity must stop sending it.

Bug Fixes

  • Reject whitespace between a header name and the colon (RFC 9112 §5.1).
  • Trim only spaces and tabs around Transfer-Encoding values (RFC 9110 §5.6.3) (#3364).
  • Reject a Content-Length that is not plain digits (RFC 9110 §8.6).
  • Reject chunk data not followed by CRLF (RFC 9112 §7.1).
  • Reject control characters in the request path (RFC 9112 §3.2) (#3371).
  • Return 414 URI Too Long for a request line over limit_request_line (RFC 9112 §3) (#2487).
  • ASGI: never write more body bytes than the app's Content-Length, and close the connection when the body is shorter (RFC 9112 §6.3).
  • ASGI: close the connection when the app returns before finishing its response (RFC 9112 §6.3).
  • ASGI: reject response header names and values that are not valid (RFC 9110 §5.1, §5.5).
  • WSGI: reject a response status that is not three digits followed by a valid reason phrase (RFC 9112 §4).

title: Optimizations Opt-In
body:
Intent of this PR is dicussed in: https://github.com/green-coding-solutions/green-metrics-tool/pull/1947

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary

This PR makes optimization analysis opt-in. The `skip_optimizations` option is replaced by `optimizations`, which defaults to `false`.

### Behavior changes

- **CLI (`runner.py`):** `--skip-optimizations` is replaced by `--optimizations`. Reporters run only when `--optimizations` is set and neither `--dev-no-save` nor `--dev-no-metrics` is set.
- **Scenario runner (`lib/scenario_runner.py`):** The constructor argument `skip_optimizations=False` becomes `optimizations=False`. It is stored as `_optimizations`.
- **Cron jobs (`lib/job/run.py`):** The job passes `optimizations` from the user's `measurement` capabilities, with default `False`. Reporters run only when `runner._optimizations` is true. Previously they ran after every run. This gate does not check `_dev_no_save` or `_dev_no_metrics`.
- **User settings (`lib/user.py`, `docker/seed-data.sql`, `frontend/settings.html`, `frontend/js/settings.js`):** `measurement.optimizations` replaces `measurement.skip_optimizations` in the updateable settings and the settings UI. The UI label changes to "Run optimizations after run."
- **Statistics page (`frontend/js/stats.js`):** Optimization data loads only when `runner_arguments.optimizations` is `true`. Otherwise, the page shows a message that optimizations were not enabled.
- **Shell runner (`shell.py`):** The forced `skip_optimizations=True` is removed.

### Migration

`migrations/2026_11_16_optimizations_opt_in.sql` contains two updates:

1. It renames `measurement.skip_optimizations` to `measurement.optimizations` in each user's `updateable_settings`.
2. For every user with a top-level `measurement` key, it removes `skip_optimizations` and sets `optimizations` to `false`.

The second update sets `optimizations` to `false` for all such users. It does not keep an existing enabled state. Users who previously had optimizations enabled (`skip_optimizations = false`) lose that state after migration.

### Scripts and documentation

- `run-template.sh`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.devcontainer/splash.md` drop `--skip-optimizations` from quick-run commands. The Bakery Demo command keeps `--skip-unsafe`.

### Tests

- Tests remove `skip_optimizations=True` from `ScenarioRunner`, `ShellScenarioRunner`, and CLI invocations. `tests/test_dependency_collection.py` uses `skip_download_dependencies=True` instead.
- `tests/test_runner.py` adds tests for `--optimizations`. It checks that reporters run, the option is stored as `True`, and optimization labels persist. Without the flag, reporters do not run and no optimization rows are stored.
- `tests/cron/test_jobs.py` adds a test that enables `measurement.optimizations` and checks that reporters run and `message_optimization` is saved.
- `tests/frontend/test_frontend.py` checks the new settings checkbox.
- `tests/test_resource_limits.py` splits the memory-`None` and CPU-`None` tests into separate functions.

### Scope

The diff covers 27 files, with 296 lines added and 207 removed. CI and test results are not available for this summary.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: (fix): NVMe disks where attributed too high bc kernel counts in 512 sectors already
body:
Code was under the assumption that read sectors had to be multiplied with native sector size.

But kernel reports already in 512 sector size, so we can use a constant

## Impact

No devices in our measurement cluster use sector sizes other than 512, so no invalid measurement data was found.

if you however run GMT with NVMe disks you might be affected and values can be 8x too high as NVMe typically has 4k sectors

title: (rework): Replaced sed -i eval with writing to temp file
body: in macOS sed -i behaved differently and we carried a workaround with eval for a long time which was error prone. Now since we got issues of writing stuff in a VM with bind mounts we finally replaced this with a wrapper. No more sed issues :) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Replaces the `sed -i` workaround in `lib/install_shared.sh` with a new helper. - Adds `sed_inplace` function. It runs `sed` into a temporary file, copies the result back into the target file, and removes the temporary file. If `sed` fails, it removes the temporary file and returns 1. - Changes `prepare_config` to call `sed_inplace` for all substitutions. Previously it called `sed -i` through `eval`, with a separate branch for macOS (`sed -i ''`). - The helper writes into the existing file instead of renaming a new file over it. The code comment states this avoids "Device or resource busy" errors on bind-mounted files, such as in VMs or containers. - The change removes the GNU and BSD `sed -i` syntax difference. Scope: one file, `lib/install_shared.sh`, with 55 lines added and 46 removed.

title: Job run isolation - Fix GMT Memory Overhead
body: Reason for this PR: Fix GMT Overhead memory growing between cluster jobs GMT Overhead memory in the cluster grew after each job and never went back down, e.g. +123 MB after a normal run and +760 MB after a 2 h run. Two things kept it in the long-running client.py process. First, the optimization reporters import scipy and FastAPI, and imported modules are never released. Second, phase_stats fetches all measurement values of a run at once, and the freed libpq buffers stay in the glibc heap. - client.py now runs each job and the control workload in a short-lived child process (lib/process_isolation.py, based on ProcessPoolExecutor), so all of that memory goes back to the OS when the child exits. - Optimization reporters now load the full measurement data only if a reporter actually accesses it. No current reporter does. - ConfigurationCheckError and TemperatureException can now be pickled, so they reach client.py intact from the child. GlobalConfig remembers its file path so the child loads the same --config-override. - runner.py now adds a warning to every run when --iterations or several files run in one process, because memory there can still build up between runs. An earlier PR already tried to address this by free()-ing memory but the data was locked in to some Python extensions heaps and not pruneable. - https://github.com/green-coding-solutions/green-metrics-tool/pull/1967 ## Graphs of Memory Overheads for 20 Minute runs ## Graphs of Memory Overhad for 2 hours runs Red spikes in the graph which can go up technically indefinitely. But 1,000 MB is the biggest we have seen on the cluster ## Impact on cluster We have seen max. impacts of 1,000 MB so far. Since all our clusters have a memory reservation of 1 GB for the GMT and the host itself workloads are basically unimpacted even if they saturate the memory. However if you run your own GMT cluster and have memory reservations which are lower or run absolute memory saturating worklodas you will have data that is slightly representative of a more memory limited machine than the hardware would suggest. No CPU or energy noise should be in the data. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary This change runs cluster job processing and control workloads in child processes. Memory used by a child process returns to the operating system when the child exits. ## Changes - **`lib/process_isolation.py`(new):** Adds `run_isolated(func, *args, **kwargs)`. It runs the callable in a spawned, single-worker child process. It returns the result or re-raises the exception. The child loads the parent's config location and closes any existing `DB` instance after the callable finishes. Adds `IsolatedProcessTerminated`. The child handles SIGTERM and SIGINT. The first signal raises an exception, and later signals are ignored. - **`cron/client.py`:** Runs control workloads and job processing through `run_isolated`. After a job's child process exits, the run ID reloads in a `finally` block. - **`lib/job/run.py`:** Adds `RunJob.load_run_id()`. It reads the newest run ID for the job from the database and updates `_run_id` if a row exists. Otherwise it keeps the existing value. - **`lib/configuration_check_error.py`:** `ConfigurationCheckError` and `TemperatureException` define `__reduce__`. Pickling preserves constructor arguments and instance attributes, so exceptions can cross the process boundary. - **`lib/global_config.py`:** `override_config` sets `config_location` to the location it loads. Child processes therefore use the same config file. - **`lib/scenario_runner.py`:** `cleanup()` resets `__working_folder_rel` to an empty `Path` instead of an empty string. - **`runner.py`:** When one process schedules more than one scenario run, the runner prints a warning before each run. The warning states that retained post-processing memory can inflate GMT Overhead and other memory metrics. It recommends separate runner invocations for comparable values. A single run does not print the warning. - **`tests/test_runner.py`:** Asserts that the warning appears once per executed run. ## Scope and limits - Memory accumulation can still occur in local `--iterations` and multi-`--filename` runs. The warning covers these cases. The PR does not remove this behavior. - The PR does not change the reporters' lazy loading of measurement data, which the PR objectives describe. The raw summary does not list it as a file change. - Test and CI results: not available.

title: (rework): Moving Clock to CLOCK_REALTIME again
body: We had errors with long runs even when NTP is off. CLOCK_MONTONIC_RAW does not apply frequency correction for skewed clock crystals. This means altough _RAW clocks are immune to jumping back in time and also to NTP jumps forward they also do not get frequency corrections from the kernel. However the python timing functions get them and more problematic also any date() call inside a container uses CLOCK_REALTIME by default. We could move the whole python timings to _RAW clocks but then problems in docker containers would persist breaking all timings that users create or SCI timestamps / user created notes would produce. With NTP off there is no downside anymore to use CLOCK_REALTIME as no jumping can occur. Since the NTP feature came after the _RAW decision we now decide with new knowledge for this rollback as the better implementation. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Reverts the clock source from `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` to `CLOCK_REALTIME`, because `_RAW` does not receive kernel frequency corrections. - `lib/c/gmt-lib.c` and `.h`: removes `get_time_offset` and `get_adjusted_time`; adds `get_time(struct timeval *now)`, which reads `CLOCK_REALTIME`. Exits with `EXIT_FAILURE` on `clock_gettime` failure. - Metric providers (CPU, disk, memory, network, GPU, PSU, lmsensors, throttling): replace `get_adjusted_time` with `get_time` and remove the offset state. - Windows Scaphandre reader: uses `GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime` directly; QPC stays for sleep scheduling.

title: Bump deepdiff from 9.1.0 to 9.2.1
body:
Bumps [deepdiff](https://github.com/qlustered/deepdiff) from 9.1.0 to 9.2.1.
Release notes

Sourced from deepdiff's releases.

9.2.1

New features

  • iterable_match_keys: match list items by key per path, e.g. {"root['orders']": "order_id", "root['orders'][*]['lines']": ("sku", "warehouse")}. Paths use the exclude_paths glob syntax; a key spec is a key name, a tuple of key names, or a callable. Matching is O(n + m), inserted/removed/reordered records are reported per record at real list indexes, and Delta round-trips (#664, #666).
    • Duplicate keys pair by occurrence; items without a key pair in order.
    • 1 and 1.0 are the same key; booleans and strings never match numbers.
    • With ignore_order, keyed lists are still paired by key, without reporting moves.
    • Subtree multiprocessing falls back to serial when iterable_match_keys is used.
    • New docs page: docs/iterable_match_keys.rst.

Python support

  • Added Python 3.15 support (#661).
  • Dropped Python 3.10, which reached end-of-life in October 2026. Supported versions are now 3.11–3.15.
    • cachebox>=6.1.2,<7 (first release with cp315 wheels); numpy ~=2.5.4 on 3.12+, ~=2.4.6 on 3.11; pandas ~=3.1.1.
    • Build backend allows flit_core<5.
    • Dropped the tomli dependency; stdlib tomllib is always used.
    • CI matrix and nox sessions updated to 3.11–3.15.

Bug fixes

  • Fixed iterable_compare_func dropping an added item whose content equals an already matched item, e.g. [{"id": 1}] vs [{"id": 1}, {"id": 1}] returned {} (#665, #666).
  • Fixed missing type changes between equal-comparing items inside ordered iterables, e.g. DeepDiff([2], [2.0]) now reports the int → float change (#605, #607), thanks to Sanjays2402.
  • Fixed truncate_datetime crashing on non-truncatable types. It now applies only to datetime.datetime and datetime.time; datetime.date, timedelta and np.datetime64 values are compared exactly instead of raising AttributeError (#597, #617), thanks to SAY-5 and Sanjays2402.
  • Fixed number_to_string producing an invalid string such as 1.0+-1.0j for complex numbers with a negative imaginary part, which crashed e.g. DeepHash(1-1j, significant_digits=3) (#551, #598, #616), thanks to koriyoshi2041 and Sanjays2402.
  • Fixed Delta JSON round-trip crashing with TypeError when orjson is not installed, for list diffs that use iterable opcodes (#613), thanks to chuenchen309.
  • Fixed _dict_from_slots dropping a parent-declared mangled __slots__ attribute for a subclass instance (#506, #609), thanks to uttam12331.
  • The deep command now exits with an actionable message (pip install "deepdiff[cli]") instead of a ModuleNotFoundError traceback when the cli extra is not installed (#594, #608), thanks to uttam12331.
  • Fixed typos in docstrings and comments (#600), thanks to Labib-Bin-Salam.

Dependencies

  • Upgraded dev/test/docs/static dependencies (polars 2.1, python-dateutil 4.0, Sphinx 9.0, pytest 9.2, coverage 7.17, pydantic 2.14, etc.) and regenerated uv.lock (#667).
  • Bumped certifi to 2026.10.18 (#654) and soupsieve to 2.8.4 (#610).

Tooling and docs

  • Switched release tooling from bump2version (broken on Python 3.15) to bump-my-version.
  • Added sandboxed, monitored test runs for untrusted PRs (scripts/pr_sandbox/), with make pr-sandbox / make pr-review targets (#663).
  • Made CLAUDE.md setup-agnostic instead of hardcoding a venv path (#662).
  • Version bumped to 9.2.0; CHANGELOG, AUTHORS, README "What is new" and docs index updated. The __slots__ fix (#506) was moved from the v9-1-0 changelog section to v9-2-0, since it was merged after 9.1.0 was released.
  • Added qluster information to the docs

title: Strip trailing slash from local --uri before saving
body: Fixes #422 ## Problem A local folder passed with `--uri` is saved to `runs.uri` exactly as typed. So `--uri /path/to/repo/` and `--uri /path/to/repo` point to the same repository but get stored as two different URIs. ## Change - `lib/scenario_runner.py` (`_checkout_repository`, local-folder branch): strip trailing slashes before the URI is saved as `__clean_uri`. A bare `/` stays `/`. URL URIs are not touched. - `tests/test_runner.py`: add `test_uri_local_dir_trailing_slash_is_stored_normalized`. It runs `basic_stress.yml` with `uri=f"{GMT_DIR}/"` and checks that `runs.uri` equals `GMT_DIR`. ## Tests I ran these on Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker 29.7.0), with the setup from `.github/actions/gmt-pytest` (`install_linux.sh ... -T -L -z -f -j -d -g --nvidia-gpu --tz GMT --disable-path-security --no-elephant --no-software-view`, then `setup-test-env.py` and `start-test-containers.sh -d`). Base is `21fd2cc`, the current `main`. | Run | Result | |---|---| | New test on `main` (test only, no fix) | 1 failed: `assert '/home/user/gmt/' == '/home/user/gmt'` | | New test with the fix | 1 passed | | Fix reverted, test kept (removal control) | 1 failed, same assertion | | `pytest test_runner.py -k "uri or filename"` with the fix | 14 passed | | `pytest test_runner.py` with the fix | 65 passed, 4 skipped, 2 failed | The 2 failures in the full `test_runner.py` run also fail on unpatched `main` in the same environment, so this change doesn't cause them: - `test_docker_pull_private_image_with_credentials_succeeds` needs `GMT_TESTING_DOCKER_USER` / `GMT_TESTING_DOCKER_PAT`. - `test_optimizations_flag_runs_reporters` exits 1 in `runner.py --optimizations` in my sandbox. I did not run the rest of the suite (`test_usage_scenario.py`, `api/`, `frontend/` and so on) locally. I'm leaving those to the PR CI. `pylint lib/scenario_runner.py tests/test_runner.py` with the repo's `.pylintrc` scores 10.00/10. ## AI disclosure An AI coding agent working on my account prepared this PR: the fix, the test, the local test runs and this description. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? title: Reject quotes in repo URL on /v1/runs/add
body: Refs #382 ## Problem `POST /v1/runs/add` accepts a `repo_url` that contains `'` or `"` (e.g. `https://broken-uri'.de`) and creates the job, so the URL gets stored and later shows up in the runs / repositories views. #382 proposes rejecting these at the add endpoint, so that they never get into the DB. ## Change This follows step 1 of the proposal in #382. - `api/scenario_runner.py` (`runs_add`): right after the "URL is empty" check, return a 422 with `URL must not contain quote characters (' or ")` when `repo_url` contains `'` or `"`. The check runs before the repo lookup, so it also applies with `no_url_check=true`. - `tests/api/test_api_software_add.py`: add `test_post_run_add_repo_url_with_quotes`, parametrized over `https://broken-uri'.de`, `https://broken-uri".de` and a GitHub URL with a trailing `'`. It posts with `no_url_check=true` and expects the 422, that exact error text, and no created job. On step 2 (row identifier): I checked current `main` and the frontend no longer breaks on these URIs, so this PR leaves the frontend alone. I added two runs to the DB whose `uri` was `https://broken-uri'.de` and `https://broken-uri".de`, then used Playwright (Firefox) to open Runs / Repos, switch to the repository view and expand each row. Both rows rendered, the nested runs table loaded the run, the accordion's `data-uri` attribute read back the exact URI, and there were no page errors. `escapeString` / `encodeURIComponent` now cover these paths in `frontend/js/helpers/runs.js`. That throwaway check is not part of this PR. If you'd still like the row keyed by an id or hash, I can do it as a follow-up. ## Tests I ran these on Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker 29.7.0, Python 3.12.3), with the setup from `.github/actions/gmt-pytest`: `install_linux.sh ... -T -L -z -f -j -d -g --nvidia-gpu --tz GMT --disable-path-security --no-elephant --no-software-view`, then `setup-test-env.py` and `start-test-containers.sh -d`. The base is `96e0b5d`, the current `main`. I restarted the gunicorn test container after each source change. | Run | Result | |---|---| | New test on `main` (test only, no fix) | 3 failed: `assert 202 == 422` (job created) | | New test with the fix | 3 passed | | Check removed, test kept (removal control) | 3 failed, same assertion | | `pytest api/test_api_software_add.py` with the fix | 38 passed | | `pytest api/test_api_scenario_runner.py` with the fix | 32 passed | I did not run the rest of the suite locally. I'm leaving it to the PR CI. `pylint api/scenario_runner.py tests/api/test_api_software_add.py` scores 10.00/10. ## AI disclosure An AI coding agent working on my account prepared this PR: the fix, the test, the local test runs and this description. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
